weather_adaptations.description: Pacific Northwest conditions (heavy rain, high moisture, occasional cold) require specific habits.
rain_and_wet_conditions: Use heavy-duty rubber floor mats or bed liner material on the cargo floor: easier to clean and protects against constant wet boots and equipment.
Stage a small dirty zone near the rear doors when practical so you are not tracking mud and water the full length of the van.
cold_weather: Keep a small jump pack or spare batteries. Cold drains batteries faster.
Hand warmers and a decent scraper belong in the cab during winter months.
weather_adaptations.moisture_management_in_van: Good airflow when parked (when safe) and periodic deep cleaning help prevent the van itself from becoming a mold source during wet periods.

van_cleaning_and_maintenance.periodic_deep_clean: Every van accumulates fine dust over time from jobs. Do not let it build up until the van looks neglected.
van_cleaning_and_maintenance.recommended_technique: Use a leaf blower on low or run a dry ULV (no liquid) through the cargo area periodically. This quickly knocks accumulated dust out of shelving, equipment, corners, and racking. Follow up with a quick vacuum on the floor if needed.
van_cleaning_and_maintenance.frequency: Every 1–2 weeks depending on job types, or anytime visible dust buildup appears.

professional_appearance.note: Customers will occasionally see inside your van. What they see should look like a professional workshop, not a stinking trash fire. A clean, organized van builds trust even before you start the job.

comfort_and_quality_of_life.note: If you have the space and want to make long days in the van more tolerable, consider adding a few basic comforts.
practical_options: Small microwave or single-burner hot plate: these can usually run off the alternator through a quality inverter or from job site power when available.
Compact fridge or cooler: these generally require more consistent power. Better suited to an auxiliary battery + solar setup if you want reliable operation when the engine is off.
Regular cooler with ice or frozen water bottles for hot weather: cheap, no power draw, and effective for drinks and food.
considerations: Space and weight trade-offs are real. Only add what you will actually use regularly.
Any inverter setup should be properly fused and wired.
Keep food storage and cooking areas clean and separated from work zones to avoid contamination issues.

daily_reset_habits.description: A realistic daily reset prevents the van from becoming a mess over time. By the end of most days you’re tired, so keep the evening reset practical and sensible.
evening_minimum: Get everything back into its general zone so nothing is loose or rolling around.
Remove obvious trash if it’s easy. Full trash dump can often wait until morning if you have a dumpster at the shop.
Quick visual check that high-value items are secured.
daily_reset_habits.morning_reset: Morning is often a better time for a slightly deeper clean and reset. Use it to also do a quick stock/consumables check against the day’s expected scope. Be sensible about what actually keeps the van functional and professional for your situation.
daily_reset_habits.overall_goal: Prevent the van from slowly turning into a contaminated, disorganized rolling mess without demanding perfection every single evening when you’re already worn out.

van_organization.voice_considerations: Keep it practical and slightly opinionated where real field experience supports it. Focus on time savings, reduced frustration, professionalism, and liability protection. Most techs already have some system: the goal is to make it intentional and consistent while staying realistic about fatigue and real-world constraints.

field_adaptations.title: Field Adaptations
field_adaptations.description: Real-world, practical improvisations used by restoration techs. Only includes fixes that actually make sense in the field. Also the primary parking place for rare edge-case lessons that would otherwise be forgotten until the next expensive recurrence.
field_adaptations.core_principle: Improvising is a valuable skill, but only when it’s realistic. Some things are worth driving back to the shop for.
trigger_phrases: we better go back to the shop

field_fixes.solution: Jam two screwdrivers into the drain slots in opposite directions to create torque
Cut the bolts off with a Sawzall high enough to avoid damaging the toilet base
Tape 4 mil or 6 mil plastic together to form a tube
field_fixes.result: Makeshift layflat created on the spot

field_fixes.solution: Twist duct tape into a tight roll with the sticky side facing outward
Tape a HEPA filter to a box fan or cut a hole in containment and pull air through the filter
field_fixes.guard: Not for Category 3, asbestos, or mold disturbance. Prefer a real NAM/AFD. Improvised HEPA+box-fan is a clean-job stopgap only.
field_fixes.voice_note: HEPA taped to a box fan can buy basic negative on a clean job, not for Cat 3, asbestos, or mold disturbance. Prefer a real NAM or AFD.

field_fixes.solution: Use a screw, nail, or knife to scratch your mark into the material
Use a 5-gallon bucket to carry your tools
field_fixes.result: Simple and effective mobile tool storage

field_fixes.problem: Drywall sheet stuck behind non-removable water heater: screws still grip even when panel is loose and broken
field_fixes.solution: Make a lasso from twine, rolled tape, wire, or insulation. Feed it over the top, loop around the backside, drop down, cinch tight, and pull the sheet straight up and out from behind the heater
field_fixes.result: Extracts the stubborn piece cleanly without needing to move the water heater

field_fixes.problem: Snapping a chalk line alone, with no second person to hold the far end
field_fixes.solution: Put your knife blade through the hook ring on the end of the chalk line and stick the knife into the wall at your first mark. Pull the line all the way across to your other mark and snap it yourself

water_interception.pattern: When water is still coming, don't fight it where it lands. Catch it and give it a path: tape and plastic make a bib, slide, or channel that routes water to one spot you control; out a door, into a container, or to the extractor.
water_interception.status: Pattern, not policy. Adapt it to what's on site.

examples.situation: Front-load washer overfilled; water standing behind the door glass.
examples.setup: Vinyl tape (not duct tape: duct tape can strip paint) bibbed across the front of the machine below the door. A plastic sheet taped to the bib as a slide, run out the door or to where you can catch it.
examples.sequence: Staged opening: open the door a little, let it run or scoop, close, repeat until the water is below the door lip. Then the extractor for the rest.
examples.watch_for: Gaps in the framing between the door opening and the taped area can let water into the machine base. Tape the gap and drain again.

examples.situation: Large commercial building; ceiling breach with water still coming through.
examples.setup: Plastic set up as a rain-catch channel under the breach, sloped to route the water to one collection point.
examples.sequence: Catch, route, collect. Keep emptying or extracting at the collection point until the breach is covered or the water stops.
examples.watch_for: A sag turns into a pocket that tears under the weight. Keep the slope running to the collection point.

water_interception.voice_note: Still coming in? Catch it and give it a path: tape and plastic to one collection point, then extract.

field_adaptations.voice_considerations: Before you say we don’t have something, tell me what we *do* have. Some things you can improvise, some things you need to just go back to the shop and get. Knowing the difference is part of being a good tech.

edge_case_memory.principle: If a missing tool or sequence cost the crew hours and is unlikely to be remembered months later, it belongs here as a short voice note.
examples_of_notes_to_add: The one tool that is almost never carried but occasionally saves an entire day of labor.
Access or extraction tricks that only appear on certain construction types.
Coordination sequences with plumbers or abatement that only happen on heavy sewage or specialty losses.

technology.title: Technology
technology.description: Technology set: field technology RestoKit has tried or is exploring; remote job-site monitoring hardware, smart glasses, voice capture, timestamp sync, time logs, jobsite connectivity, and fleet topology. Source of truth for the company board Manual/Lookup Technology dropdown.

containment.rule: Not on the daily field path. Morning review, day-forward, phase guidance, moisture, equipment, and job analysis for regular techs do not load, cite, or suggest this module. Shown only in the Manual/Lookup Technology set.
containment.not_this: Not office-server or board systems status. This module only records connection points.
containment.source_docs: Supporting notes stay with the company; they are not in this file.

remote_monitoring_hardware.label: Remote monitoring: Raspberry Pi / OtterBox / sensors
remote_monitoring_hardware.status: exploration: premium service concept, not a kit default
remote_monitoring_hardware.summary: A Raspberry Pi in an OtterBox with breadboard attachments and job-site sensors logs drying data continuously between visits, without opening the chamber or disturbing the home. Gear data comes in over dehumidifier Bluetooth; readings leave over house Wi‑Fi or a drive-up Starlink connection when the house has power but no Wi‑Fi. Headline outputs: continuous timestamped spreadsheet logging from screw probes (Continuous Timestamped Spreadsheet Logging); Starlink field utility for job file access and photo sharing (Technology: Topics: Always-on Jobsite Network: Starlink Field Utility).
why: Bound moisture in framing/subfloor dries slowly; daily trips to read it waste time.
Long travel time to far jobs.
Privacy / non-disturbance: customers who don't want daily visits (illness, policy, schedule).
Continuous curve instead of visit snapshots; catches gear shut off overnight.
hardware: Raspberry Pi in a sealed OtterBox, breadboard/prototyping attachments.

Bound-moisture probes: stainless screws driven into framing members, wired to the board; the Pi reads conductivity/resistance between screws like a pin meter. Needs an ADC, species/temperature correction, and calibration against a pin meter on site.
Temp/RH sensors inside and outside the chamber for GPP and dew point.
Bluetooth (or similar) to site equipment that exposes data: run hours, inlet/outlet, power state.
Site outlet power with battery backup; uplink via Starlink, truck hotspot, or customer Wi-Fi with permission.
remote_monitoring_hardware.data: Timestamped readings logged in real time with source 'sensor'; alerts for RH rising, gear off, or probe values flat/rising. Supplements documented visit readings; does not replace them.
remote_monitoring_hardware.premium: Add-on tier: remote monitoring, fewer visits, daily drying report. Open: carrier acceptance, unit cost, install/removal labor, data ownership, consent form.
next_steps: Bench prototype: two screws in a wet/dry stud vs a pin meter.
Survey which site gear has Bluetooth data.
remote_monitoring_hardware.source_doc: Supporting notes stay with the company; they are not in this file.

continuous_logging.label: CONTINUOUS TIMESTAMPED SPREADSHEET LOGGING: Pi screw probes (invasive moisture meters), frequent rate, long period
continuous_logging.summary: This is the main point of the screw probes: the Pi reads the wired invasive probes on a fixed, frequent schedule and writes every reading to a real, consistent spreadsheet with timestamps, over the whole drying period (days to weeks). It is NOT just a snapshot of job data for the job file. Visit snapshots still go in the job file; the continuous spreadsheet is the full record behind them.

contrast.visit_snapshot: Snapshot: a few readings taken when someone visits, logged into the job file. Gaps between visits, timing varies by who shows up, nothing recorded overnight or on weekends.
contrast.continuous: Continuous: same probe, same spot, same depth, every 15–60 min (set per job), 24/7 for the whole dry. Shows the full drying curve, stalls, rebounds, and gear-off or power-loss periods.

output.format: Spreadsheet (CSV / Sheets / Excel), one row per reading, timestamped.
output.rate: Frequent: default every 15 min; never longer than 60 min.
output.period: Start of drying through dry standard, every day, no gaps.
output.use: Export into the job file as supporting documentation; graph the drying curve; defend dry time and scope.

continuous_logging.manual_note: Manual: show this field as its own heading under Remote monitoring hardware. Do not fold it into Screw Probes.

screw_probes.label: Screw probes: invasive moisture meter
screw_probes.summary: Stainless screws driven into framing members act as invasive (pin-type) moisture meter probes. Wires run from each screw pair to the breadboard, and the Pi is programmed to read conductivity/resistance between the screws over those wires (the same thing a pin meter does) for bound moisture in studs, plates, joists, and subfloor. Main output: continuous timestamped spreadsheet logging (see Continuous Timestamped Spreadsheet Logging).
notes: Pi has no analog input: add an ADC on the breadboard.
Correct for wood species and temperature; calibrate on site against a pin meter at install.
Leave screws in place for the drying period; the Pi logs on a schedule with no one entering.
Readings stored with source 'sensor', location = framing member.

dehumidifier_bluetooth.label: Dehumidifier Bluetooth
dehumidifier_bluetooth.summary: Dehus that expose Bluetooth data (run hours, inlet/outlet temp/RH, power state, faults) are read by the van Pi in the OtterBox alongside its own sensors, so gear status logs continuously without opening the chamber.
notes: Survey which site dehus have Bluetooth or app data, and what fields they expose.
Pi pairs to the dehu on site; readings stored with source 'equipment'.
Alert on dehu off, fault, or rising inlet RH (catches customer shutoffs).

connectivity_paths.label: Connection paths: Wi‑Fi or drive-up Starlink
connectivity_paths.wifi: With customer permission, the Pi uplinks over house Wi‑Fi and syncs continuously to the office database.
connectivity_paths.drive_up_starlink: Not Wi‑Fi-only. With electricity only and no house Wi‑Fi, the crew drives up with Starlink, connects remotely to the Pi OtterBox setup, pulls every reading (probes, temp/RH, dehu Bluetooth log), and leaves: no entry, no opening the chamber.
connectivity_paths.offline_buffer: Pi logs locally the whole time; whichever path connects next syncs the backlog.
connectivity_paths.starlink_field_utility: Starlink is more than the drive-up dip-out: on site it gives every tech job file access and quick photo sharing between techs so the team works efficiently. Full text: Technology: Topics: Always-on Jobsite Network: Starlink Field Utility.

smart_glasses.label: Smart glasses: BleeqUp Ranger
smart_glasses.equipment: BleeqUp Ranger AI Sports Camera Glasses (Bluetooth to phone)
good_for: Hands-free RestoKit, music, and phone while staying aware of surroundings.
limits: No framing control, so not for precise documentation; Encircle photos still come from the phone.
Must come off for mask or dirty work.
About 3 hours of continuous battery; USB-C power bank helps.
smart_glasses.alternative: Safety glasses + DeWalt Bluetooth headphones: about 80% of the benefit for 10% of the price, double as ear protection, disposable. Glasses for customer-facing work; headphones for louder/dirtier jobs.
smart_glasses.company_documentation_possibility: Optional voice/audio channel into voice capture; glasses photos are situational until a phone photo exists; glasses video is not uploaded to the job file by default unless the customer was told.
smart_glasses.source_doc: Supporting notes stay with the company; they are not in this file.

voice_capture.label: Voice capture (iOS app)
voice_capture.summary: Voice stream is the raw record: every spoken note timestamped and tied to day and job. Day log and job files are built from it by approval, not a second write-up. Transcripts are small; keep audio 30–90 days. Unmatched notes go to an inbox cleared at end of day; originals never edited.
voice_capture.source_doc: Supporting notes stay with the company; they are not in this file.

timestamp_sync.label: Photo ↔ audio ↔ text ↔ moisture sync
timestamp_sync.status: core matcher built (RestoKitCore TimeMatcher ≤10 s, SpokenReadingParser)
timestamp_sync.summary: A photo's EXIF time is matched to the voice segment said at the same moment; the transcript and any spoken or shown reading join that record. One capture feeds day log, job file, and readings table with no double entry. Readings are proposed for lead review.
timestamp_sync.source_doc: Supporting notes stay with the company; they are not in this file.

time_logs.label: Time logs
time_logs.summary: Time row needs date, tech, crew, job, clock in/out, arrival/leave per site, notes. Spoken time events and photo EXIF can fill it; open rows flagged at end of day; weekly timesheet export.
time_logs.source_doc: Supporting notes stay with the company; they are not in this file.

jobsite_connectivity.label: Always-on jobsite network
jobsite_connectivity.status: outline: field-ops requirement; premium option for no-signal sites
jobsite_connectivity.summary: Documentation standards in restoration need a signal at all times so techs in different rooms or the crawl share the file live (crawl photo goes in the file and the tech upstairs sees it right away). Options: phone/truck hotspot, Starlink, customer Wi-Fi, DIY local Bluetooth/Wi-Fi hotspot, repeater into crawl/basement. Drive-up Starlink also reaches a remote-monitoring Pi on a site with power but no Wi‑Fi (see Technology: Topics: Remote Monitoring: Connection Paths: Drive Up Starlink). Starlink field utility (job file access + quick photo sharing between techs): see Starlink Field Utility.
jobsite_connectivity.source_doc: Supporting notes stay with the company; they are not in this file.

starlink_field_utility.label: Starlink field utility: job file access + quick photo sharing between techs
starlink_field_utility.summary: Starlink is not only for electricity-only drive-up Pi reads. On company field work it is the crew's signal: every tech can open the job file on site and share photos with each other in seconds, so the team works from the same live file instead of waiting to get back to the van or office.

uses.job_file_access: Open the job file on site (scope, prior readings, photos, notes, moisture maps) from any room, the crawl, or the van: no driving off to find signal.
uses.quick_photo_sharing: Tech in the crawl snaps a photo and it lands in the file / team thread right away; the lead or PM upstairs sees it and makes the call without walking down.
uses.team_efficiency: Fewer trips between rooms, fewer repeat photos, decisions made on the spot, live coordination between techs, lead, and PM.
uses.remote_monitor_drive_up: Electricity only, no house Wi‑Fi: drive up, connect to the Pi, pull every reading, leave (Technology: Topics: Remote Monitoring: Connection Paths: Drive Up Starlink).
uses.pi_uplink: Same dish can be the Pi's uplink while the crew is on site, so the continuous log syncs to the office database.

starlink_field_utility.when_to_use: No cell signal, weak signal in basements/crawls, rural sites, multi-tech jobs where photos must move fast, or any job where the file needs to stay live.
starlink_field_utility.limits: Needs power and sky view for the dish; pair with a repeater or local hotspot to reach crawl/basement. Customer Wi‑Fi only with permission.

fleet_topology.label: Fleet topology: Pi per van, office database
fleet_topology.summary: One Raspberry Pi per van buffers site data and syncs up to one office server with a backup database when it has an uplink. The Pi path feeds the office server and the ops board.
fleet_topology.source_doc: Supporting notes stay with the company; they are not in this file.

insurance_dynamics.title: Insurance Dynamics
insurance_dynamics.description: Real-world dynamics between restoration companies and insurance carriers. This module covers how carriers typically approach claims and the practical pressures technicians and PMs face in the field.
key_realities: Insurance carriers are profit-driven businesses whose primary incentive is to minimize claim payouts.
Carriers frequently challenge slow leaks as 'neglect' or 'lack of maintenance'.
Adjusters vary significantly in technical knowledge. Some are sharp, many are not.
Experienced adjusters look at bound moisture in wood to determine leak duration. Many others only look at surface moisture readings.
Non-invasive moisture meters only read approximately ¾ inch deep. After a day or two of drying, surface readings can appear normal even when significant moisture remains deeper in the material.
Because of these gaps in understanding, selective or smoothed moisture readings are extremely common throughout the industry.
In practice, enforcement on inaccurate moisture documentation is uneven: that describes the industry, not permission. Falsified readings are fraud exposure for the tech and the company.
insurance_dynamics.field_reality: The current system creates strong incentives for both carriers and contractors to bend the rules. Many companies have normalized certain documentation practices because enforcement is weak and the financial pressure is high.
practical_guidance: Record actual moisture readings; never invent or smooth numbers for the file. Document moisture readings honestly and consistently.
Take clear photos of all affected areas before and during demo.
When expanding scope, prioritize visible evidence and clear water migration patterns over moisture meter readings alone.
Be prepared to clearly explain your reasoning when challenged.
Understand that many adjusters will not catch subtle technical details on their own.
insurance_dynamics.voice_considerations: When speaking with customers, be transparent that insurance companies have strict rules and limitations. When speaking with adjusters, remain calm, professional, and fact-based.

honesty_guard.rule: Never falsify moisture readings. Always document the real numbers for the file and the carrier. Field reality that smoothed readings are common is not permission to fake readings.
honesty_guard.voice_note: Document the real numbers. Never falsify moisture readings for the file or the carrier.

policy_rule.rule: The restorer does not interpret the customer's policy. Coverage questions go to the carrier or the customer's agent. Mold and bacteria are commonly excluded: say so as a general fact, not a coverage opinion.
policy_rule.voice_note: I can't tell you what your policy covers: that's your adjuster or agent. I can tell you what the job needs and document it.

insurance_dynamics.coverage_limitation: Coverage is a job condition, not just a billing detail. Determining what the policy will and will not pay for is required up front; mold or regulated-material exclusions can turn into a limitation or complication that is written and noticed (Legal and Liability: Limitations Complexities Complications Conflicts).

monitoring.title: Monitoring
monitoring.description: Dedicated daily monitoring protocols, fixed-point measurement methods, trend documentation discipline, and special handling for long-dwell or contaminated drying situations. This module exists because daily monitoring is one of the most commonly skipped yet highest-value tasks in restoration.
monitoring.core_principle: Daily monitoring is non-negotiable. Missing daily readings cannot be accurately recreated later: this forces techs to either admit poor performance or fabricate data. Company-wide uniformity in monitoring method is more important than which specific method is chosen. Proper daily monitoring protects the job file, supports billing, and prevents callbacks.
key_principles: Daily monitoring is one of the most commonly skipped tasks in the industry.
Missing daily readings cannot be accurately recreated later: this forces techs to either admit poor performance or fabricate data.
Proper daily monitoring must be treated as non-negotiable.
Company-wide uniformity in monitoring method is more important than which specific method is chosen.

screw_method.name: The Screw Method
screw_method.description: Install two screws into the wettest spot (or a representative elevated area). Take daily pin-type moisture readings directly off the screws. This creates repeatable fixed points and eliminates reliance on fragile or inconsistent hammer probes.
advantages: Works on wood, drywall, and many other materials
screw_method.voice_note: Screw method on the wettest spot: two screws, same depth every day. Readings come right off the screws so we’re comparing apples to apples.

crawlspace_wire_extension.name: Crawlspace Wire Extension
crawlspace_wire_extension.description: Run speaker wire, thermostat wire, or similar from the monitoring screws out through the crawlspace access so daily pin readings can be taken from outside without repeated full entries. Highly effective for tight, nasty, or long-dwell crawlspaces.
crawlspace_wire_extension.best_for: Low-clearance, contaminated, or physically difficult crawlspaces where daily entry is undesirable.
crawlspace_wire_extension.voice_note: On nasty crawls I run wire from the screws out to the access so I can take readings without climbing all the way back in every day.

chasing_the_wettest_spot.name: Chasing the Wettest Spot
chasing_the_wettest_spot.description: When the original measurement point dries out or is no longer representative, move the screws (or create new ones) to the current wettest area and clearly document the change in location and rationale. Never pretend the old point is still valid.
chasing_the_wettest_spot.documentation_requirement: Note the date, old location, new location, and reason for move in the daily log.
chasing_the_wettest_spot.voice_note: The original spot dried, so I moved the screws to the new wettest area today and logged it. We track the actual worst-case moisture, not a fixed point that’s no longer wet.

integration.notes: This module provides the detailed 'how' for the monitoring steps referenced in Phase 3 and the Drying and Monitoring module. Use the fixed-point techniques during every daily monitoring visit. Which note to stage is Visit Note Cadence. Fill path for materials and meter lines is the company materials-and-readings skill.

materials_in_play.rule: Check logged-current materials only. Do not prompt to add a new material by default. The user may elect to add one.
materials_in_play.daily: Moisture is taken daily on each material currently in play, at the same points.
materials_in_play.same_day_exposure: A layer just opened is logged the same day, layer by layer. That is a Scope (and room SOL, when it is the source) entry. It is not a prompt to invent extra monitoring points.
materials_in_play.hydro_ids: Do not invent Hydro point IDs. A needle or display estimate from a photo is not a Hydro point unless it was logged there.
materials_in_play.tramex_wood_timber_max: Tramex Moisture Encounter Wood/Timber scale max is 30. Pegged right is MAXED at 30. A reading around 25 is near the ceiling, not mid-range. Do not mix that scale with Tramex Drywall/Plaster.

monitoring.voice_considerations: Monitoring is where good jobs become defensible jobs. Keep the language practical and repetitive: the same structure every day builds the habit. Emphasize that the data protects everyone.
test_intake_lines: Moisture content is a percent of oven-dry weight, and only if the meter is calibrated for that material and temperature. Otherwise it is a moisture level. A sensor is not a meter.
Low-evaporation materials are plaster, wood, concrete, and masonry. Low-evaporation assemblies include multilayer wallboard, multilayer subfloors, and gym floors.

mold_cleaning.title: Mold Cleaning
mold_cleaning.description: There is no single correct way to clean mold. Different companies and technicians use different methods with acceptable results. Physical removal is generally more important than the specific chemical used. A common practical approach is to HEPA vacuum, then wipe (with a botanical disinfectant only when a biocide line is approved: label), then follow with a light mist of stain remover (MMR) applied with a spray bottle and scrubbed with a wire brush. Apply stain remover sparingly and evenly to avoid streaking. Some technicians prefer to let the wood dry before applying products for better penetration, while others apply while damp with no noticeable difference in final results. In heavily contaminated spaces an approved, label-allowed ULV application can supplement the work after physical cleaning: it never replaces HEPA vacuum and wipe. Notify the customer of strong chemical odors before beginning. The goal is clean, stain-free, odor-free surfaces rather than surgical-suite sterility.
mold_cleaning.core_principle: Physical removal matters more than the specific chemical. Prefer wipe, scrub, vacuum, and controlled mist over chemistry-as-cleanup. Goal is clean, stain-free, odor-free surfaces, not surgical-suite sterility.
mold_cleaning.customer_notify: Notify the customer before strong chemical odors (oxidizers, stain removers, heavy fog). Mask up when serum/oxidizer burns sinuses.

cleaning_stacks.rule: Never move dust onto a surface already cleaned. Each step's mess is the next step's target.

punchlist_demo.guidance: Demo finishes before the stack starts. Trim edges neat, pull fasteners (nails/screws/staples), clear corners and missed sections, then vacuum. Do not breeze past punchlist demo into cleaning.
punchlist_demo.voice_note: Punchlist demo first: trim edges, pull the fasteners, clear the corners, then vacuum. The stack starts after demo is actually done.

sequence: Spray (approved biocide line only, per label; otherwise a detailed wipe)
pre_dryout.voice_note: Pre-dryout stack: vacuum, blow inside containment, vacuum, spray if a biocide is approved (otherwise wipe), then one drying phase. Don't spray into a dust pile.
pre_dryout.blow_note: Blowing (air washing) is done only inside a controlled chamber with HEPA capture running, never as open air movement through the house.

sequence: Optional fog only if a biocide line is approved
Final check: visual, odor, towel wipe, dry
post_dryout.reason: Fans already moved air during dryout. No blow. No second dry.
post_dryout.voice_note: Post-dryout: HEPA vacuum, wipe. Fog only if a biocide is approved, then wipe the settled residue. Finish on the check: look, smell, towel wipe, dry. No blow, no second dry.

fog_rule.guidance: Fog is flash-off, not a bath. Light mist, gone in hours. If you soak the deck, you blew the sequence.
fog_rule.voice_note: Fog is flash-off, not a bath. Light mist: gone in hours. Soak the deck and you blew the sequence.

wipe_gate.guidance: Wipe before any final fog so chemistry lands on a clean surface, and wipe settled mist residue after it. Knockdown residue is not the return to Condition 1.
wipe_gate.voice_note: Wipe before the final fog: chemistry on surface, not on dust.

cleaning_stacks.voice_note: Never move dust onto a surface you already cleaned. Pre-dryout: vacuum, blow inside controlled containment, vacuum, spray only if approved; one dry. Post-dryout: vacuum, wipe, fog only if approved, wipe the residue, then the check. No blow, no second dry.

practical_approach.wipe_then_mist: A common practical approach: HEPA vacuum, then wipe, with a rag soaked in botanical disinfectant only when a biocide line is approved (per label), then, if the client wants it, a light mist of stain remover (MMR) with a spray bottle, scrub with a wire brush. Apply stain remover sparingly and evenly to avoid streaking.
practical_approach.timing: Some techs prefer wood dry before products for penetration; others apply while damp with no noticeable difference in final results.
practical_approach.heavy_load: In heavily contaminated spaces an approved, label-allowed ULV application can supplement the work after physical soil is removed: it never replaces HEPA vacuum and wipe (fog is not removal).
practical_approach.serum_oxidizer: Oxidizer serum burns sinuses: mask on. Uneven application streaks. Spray bottom-up on verticals. Damp, not dripping.
practical_approach.stain_remover_note: Stain remover (MMR-type) is cosmetic. It goes on only after the growth is physically removed, and only if the client wants it.

mold_cleaning.voice_note: Physical removal first: chemistry second. Notify the customer of strong odors. Goal is clean, stain-free, odor-free, not a surgical suite.

moisture_after_spray_note.guidance: After spray in the cleaning stack, do not surface-meter immediately: chemistry fools the meter. See Drying and Monitoring: Moisture Readings After Spray.
moisture_after_spray_note.voice_note: Just sprayed? Don't surface-meter yet: wait for flash-off or probe the framing.

spore_reservoir.title: Spore Reservoir
spore_reservoir.guidance: Drying stops the bloom; it does not clear the reservoir. Mold goes dormant, not dead. Spores and some hyphae wait for moisture and food. A leftover strip on a 360-opened wall is a closed cavity that can sit quiet for years until someone opens it: callback cost is a second mobilization, not just the minutes to cut the strip now.
spore_reservoir.voice_note: Drying stops the bloom: it doesn't clear the reservoir. Mold goes dormant, not dead. Don't leave a strip on a 360-opened wall: that's a closed cavity waiting to callback.

kill_then_remove.title: Remove, Don't Just Kill
kill_then_remove.guidance: Do not spray products on mold and call it done. Kill is not remove: dead spores and fragments remain a reservoir. Physical removal is the primary means. If you cannot remove it right away: contain locally so nothing spreads, then physically remove. A lock-down mist to cut dust during removal is optional and its residue is cleaned; it is never the remediation. Spray, fog, or coat without removal is a written deviation.
kill_then_remove.voice_note: Don't spray mold and call it done: kill is not remove. If you can't pull it now: contain it, then physically remove it. A mist just knocks dust down; the residue gets wiped.

condition_labels.title: Condition Labels

Condition 2.definition: Residue from known growth in that building: spores and fragments off a Condition 3 mass.

Condition 3.definition: Actual growth, hidden included. Visible growth is Condition 3.

condition_labels.retired_labels: Normal, Settled, and Colonized are not the speakable labels. No one-to-one map. Settled is the weak fit: an inactive look is not Condition 2.
condition_labels.assumption_rule: Assuming a condition is written, with the rationale.
condition_labels.voice_note: Call the surface Condition 1, 2, or 3. Do not say Normal, Settled, or Colonized.

ale.title: Additional Living Expense (ALE) / Loss of Use
ale.description: ALE (often Coverage D, loss of use) is commonly claimable when a covered loss makes the home uninhabitable: hotel or temporary housing, meals above normal grocery costs, laundry, pet boarding, storage. Whether it applies is the carrier's or agent's call, not the restorer's (Insurance Dynamics: Policy Rule). Anticipate it during Phase 1 by evaluating kitchen and bathroom access. Communicate potential ALE impact to the insurance adjuster and agent as early as possible. Early documentation that the home is uninhabitable strengthens defensibility when justifying longer equipment runtimes or project duration.
ale.deferred_reason: Title+description only: full ALE workflow tree deferred; not field-critical for core drying runtime.
ale.voice_note: Flag ALE early if the home is uninhabitable: kitchen/bath access drives hotel and meal spend; tell the adjuster soon.

electricity_bills.title: Electricity Bill Increases
electricity_bills.description: Running drying equipment 24/7 can cause a noticeable spike in electric bills, especially in smaller homes with low normal usage. The increase is often claimable, but coverage is the adjuster's or agent's call: do not promise it (Insurance Dynamics: Policy Rule). Tell the homeowner up front that equipment will use power, and give them the usage record from the Pre-Setup Power Survey so they can claim reimbursement from their insurer. Crews do not document the homeowner's baseline bills or quote a power company's rate. Carriers typically want baseline documentation, either the current bill compared to the same month from the previous year, or several recent months of bills to establish normal usage.
electricity_bills.deferred_reason: Title+description only: bill-spike claim workflow deferred; keep as a thin reference (the homeowner handles baseline bills and the claim with their insurer). The usage record for the homeowner lives in the Pre-Setup Power Survey.
electricity_bills.voice_note: Equipment can spike the electric bill. Tell the homeowner up front, and give them the usage record from the power survey. That is between the homeowner and their insurer: the homeowner documents baseline bills (same month last year or recent bills) and applies their power company's rate for reimbursement.

_structure_note.description: Maintainer note. Demolition, crawlspaces, and Special Situations are shallow trees. Pump-truck response is its own module (Pump Truck Deployment and Heavy Sewage Extraction). Meta and Kit Framework frame RestoKit as a field memory tool for rare edge cases.

job_type_gate.title: Job-Type Gate
job_type_gate.description: Asks what kind of job this is before any water module loads. Not every job is a water job; a remove-and-replace crawl skips category, psychrometry, and the drying stack.
job_type_gate.rule: Not every job is a water job. Ask what the work is before loading water modules (category, psychrometry, drying stack).
job_type_gate.example: Remove-and-replace crawl (insulation / visqueen / plastic vapor barrier material): no category, no psychrometry, no drying stack.
job_type_gate.voice_note: Not every job is a water job. Ask what the work is before you load category, psychrometry, and the drying stack. Remove-and-replace crawl? Skip the water modules.

answer_rules.title: Answer Rules
answer_rules.description: How RestoKit answers, in text or voice, for any level.
always_on: Safety overrides first (see Safety and Health: Voice Safety Overrides).
Job type gate before loading the water stack (see Job-Type Gate).

When a topic depends on the state, ask once what state they work in and remember it (Kit Framework: Runtime Contracts: Jurisdiction). Until then, stay state-neutral. Do not assume Oregon or any other state.
Short and direct. Lead with the call, then the why. One clarifying question at most when the answer depends on it.
Say which tier a line is when it matters: required, expected, recommended, or informative.
For any question about the standards themselves, use Kit Info: Standards Alignment and Legal and Liability: Must Not Claim. Never say the kit or the job is certified or approved.
No medical advice, no policy interpretation, no legal opinion: refer out and say who to ask.
Never suggest smoothing, inventing, or backfilling readings.
When the kit and the job disagree, the tech decides; remind them to write the deviation.

depth_modes.tech: Default. Field-ready, one to three sentences, numbers when they matter.
depth_modes.deep: On request: the science and the why. Point to the kit's own section path for the line, such as base_science.<section> or <module>.<key>.
depth_modes.rookie: On request or when the user is new: plain words, one step at a time, explain the term once.
depth_modes.pm_estimator: Scope, sequence, documentation, and change-order framing; what to write in the file.

answer_rules.mode_switching: Switch on a plain request ('go deeper', 'explain like I'm new', 'PM view'). PM view is a way of looking at the job, not a title you wait for (Leadership and Labor: PM on Site). Return to tech mode after.

safety_and_health.title: Safety and Health
safety_and_health.description: Thin stop module. Not a phase. Not a tree. Law first. Stops, each marked with its tier.
safety_and_health.core_principle: The safety practice is the applicable law, not either document.
stops: Bird and bat droppings are not a mold scope. Histoplasma, Cryptococcus, and hantavirus stop the job until the disease-control procedure is in place.
Asbestos, lead, silica, mercury, fuels, solvents, and the other named regulated materials stop the mold scope until the applicable handling is in place.

Asbestos-containing material (more than 1 percent) or presumed asbestos stops disturbing work. Suspect material is sampled or presumed. Licensed abatement. An owner survey does not clear demo. Pre-1978 lead and the renovation rule carry the same duty.
An illegal or dangerous condition is resolved immediately, or the work stops. A stoppage file has the reason and the events that led to it.

Containment with microbial contamination: skin and respiratory protection before entry. Respirator and a written program under 29 CFR 1910.134 if controls do not clear the air. P-100 for spores. No air-purifying respirator in an oxygen-deficient or immediately dangerous atmosphere.
Visible or suspected mold: stop the disturbing work, contain, then trained remediators under the current mold standard.
Engineering controls come first on a mold job. A reported health issue gets an independent assessor. A health question goes to a healthcare professional.
The license matches the work. Where the law requires a certification, the job does not start without it. Training alone is not the qualification.
A negative that pulls hard can backdraft a furnace or a water heater, or roll a flame out. Check the opening and the force before the air is reversed.
Lead and asbestos come before the mold scope. A load-bearing removal is an engineer's call. Ozone is not the removal.
Sagging ceiling board, a fire exit, an elevator pit, a permit-required confined space, and a submerged panel are stops. Asbestos removal and sprinkler work are specialist calls.
Exposed tack strip is covered. Unsanitary water takes the tack strip out with the appropriate protection and disposal.
Deteriorated ammunition is a call to police or a bomb squad. A firearm is not handled by someone who does not know the protocol.
The label is followed. A method not on the label is not used. The label and the safety data sheet go to the client before the product is used.
safety_and_health.voice_note: Law first. Regulated material stops the scope. A health question is not answered on site.
safety_and_health.tier_note: Most stops are required (law or regulation). Some come from informative starting numbers or expected practice, and the kit treats them as stops on purpose: the tack strip stop (Base Science: Material Behavior: Reference Lines, informative), the sagging ceiling and elevator pit stop (Demolition: Decision Logic: Material Decision Matrix, assemblies), the firearm stop (expected).
additional_stops: Respirator use needs the written program: NIOSH-approved selection, medical evaluation, fit testing, and training before wearing (29 CFR 1910.134). Required.
Hazard communication: written program, labels, SDS, and training before a chemical is used; on a multi-employer site, other employers are told what is in use. Required.
Permit-required confined space: no entry without the posted permit, atmospheric monitoring, and a trained entry team. Required.
Direct-fired heaters only with ventilation adequate for carbon monoxide; indirect-fired exhaust goes outside; CO is monitored while combustion equipment runs. Required / expected.
A wet electrical system stays off until a qualified person clears it. A submerged breaker is replaced. Required.
A fire-exit stair is not blocked during occupied hours unless officials clear it. Required.
A hole cut in a fire-rated wall is closed back to the rating. Required.
Hazards (structure, shock, gas) are handled before entry. Required.
crew_practices: Daily tailgate on the work and the safety issues. PPE matched to the area, inspected before use. Coveralls and shoe covers on before the containment line.
No eating, drinking, or smoking in the work area. Gear off and hands washed before breaks and at the end of the day. Damaged gloves discarded; disposable gloves leave with the debris.
Cuts treated promptly around sewage. Know the eyewash location and the emergency exits. Injuries reported to the supervisor as soon as possible.
Immunizations (tetanus/diphtheria, hepatitis A and B) are a physician referral: recommended. Immunocompromised workers are usually kept off wet contaminated work; that is a physician's call.
Heat: attics, crawls, and full PPE are heat-risk work. Hot dry skin and sudden collapse is heatstroke: emergency care now. Buddy system in heat.

rules: Never skip a safety gate to save time.
Category 3, visible mold, or a strong musty odor: PPE and containment before intrusive work.
Interrupt an unsafe action immediately, even mid-answer.
Confirm engineering controls before demo in a contaminated area. On extraction: PPE and floor protection first; containment first only when the situation calls for it.
A health question is not answered on site; it goes to a healthcare professional.

estimating.title: Estimating
estimating.description: Reference for Phase 0 (Survey & Estimate). The sales walk often happens before Phase 1, sometimes by a person who will not run the job.
estimating.core_principle: A bid is not authorization. Phase 1 still starts at signed authorization. No demo and no billable restoration scope from a bid alone.
what_is_in_it: A large loss picks cost-plus, time-and-materials, or a bid before the crew starts. Cost-plus tracks invoices plus a margin. Time-and-materials assigns costs from a price list. A bid is a measured scope. A change is a written change order signed by an authorized party and the restorer.

The estimate includes the administrator, security, rentals, and a tracking system. A draw schedule is in the contract. Out-of-state work carries that state's license and coverage. If the work state is not yet known, follow Kit Framework: Runtime Contracts: Jurisdiction.

Initial bidding is a hard job. The person pricing it often has not opened the assemblies. Hidden water, category, and dwell are easy to miss. Write what was assumed. The tech does not inherit a silent scope.
estimating.not_in_it: Unit prices, a line-item catalog, or a published price table. Those tables are licensed. The kit decides the work. The price list bills it.
field_practice: Equipment codes often carry no labor. Setup, daily monitoring, and teardown are a separate labor line.
Contents manipulation is not a pack-out. Detach-and-reset of trim, toilets, and vanities is not included in the finish line. Haul-off, floor protection, and after-hours are their own lines.
A wrong category or a short dry changes the scope. The moisture log, not the assumed two or three days, is the equipment runtime.
Removal without disposal, or carpet out without floor prep, is an incomplete pair.
Keep mitigation and rebuild as separate subtotals.
Sketch every wet room, including closets and halls. A line note names the condition, the reading, and the photo.
estimating.file_connection: Xactimate reads .esx and .chx. XML is the other platform's format. There is no public schema. Xactimate is not required by law. It is the industry default. The one real requirement is XactAnalysis: if the job came through that portal, the estimate usually has to go back through it. The structured scope is the source. The carrier PDF and the Xactimate entry are two outputs.

field_practice: kit_lines
sketch_rooms
scope_changes

estimating.voice_note: Bid is not a signature. Price what you could see, write what you assumed, and do not start the job on the bid.

large_loss.types: Commercial, industrial, institutional, complex residential. Bigger mechanical/electrical, special wiring, complex materials, more hazards.
opening_questions: Building use and who has a stake
Third parties (FEMA, EPA, health boards, HUD)
controls: Monitored fire, security, and suppression systems are controlled or shut down before work around them.
Power can be three-phase up to 480 V, not a residential circuit; generator in the plan when power is short.
Communication tree set before the crew arrives.
Security: badges, background checks under privacy law, safety watch.
Subcontracts drafted with legal help, with indemnity and the sub's own insurance.

visit_note_cadence.title: Visit Note Cadence
visit_note_cadence.description: Flags which notes to stage on a visit and opens them ready for data, using the template bodies in Note Templates. Does not write Encircle.
visit_note_cadence.core_principle: One thing done well, then the rest gets forgotten in a rush. Flag each template at its trigger and stage the structure that already exists. Surface only what this visit actually needs.
visit_note_cadence.north_star: The tool serves techs over insurance. Company procedure is the cadence these notes follow, and it is being built live. The standard rises with management attention. The social layer shows up per people and company. Pack cadence stays aligned with company process. Kit IP stays in this file.
visit_note_cadence.company_pack: Generic template bodies live in Note Templates. A company may still have its own native forms; those are recognized as aliases in Note Templates: Company Native Aliases. When this kit writes, it uses plain titles and ends every output with the ◇ resto_kit footer (Note Templates: RestoKit Tag Rule).
visit_note_cadence.encircle_boundary: Local drafts until the user says the write is OK. Route any API call through the authorized Encircle connector. Only that connector holds the token. This kit never reads or uses the token. This module offers and stages only. It never auto-writes Encircle.

templates.note: Day 0 only. Holds the native inspection fields. One per claim.
Create on first walk; update when raw capture changes.
Room note is the source; Master is a rollup only.
Single living note. Newest visit first.
Room note is the source; Master is a rollup only.
New note each visit, including Day 0.

day_0_when_called_out.when: Day 0 only when a hold, a source room, or pre-existing damage is called out.

templates.note: Create when a hold exists. Single note, not master/sub.
When found or shown. Arrival photos can already serve as preexisting-damage photos.
Moisture points every visit that takes readings, not only on drying jobs. Newest first. Check logged-current materials only.
When gear is placed, pulled, counted, or only repositioned. A wet-spot shift still gets an Equipment note: what moved, why, and how.

when_holds_or_scope_change.when: Update only when holds change or when map/demo work changes the scope. Do not push these every visit.

templates.note: Standing note. Edit in place when a hold changes.
Living room scopes; Master refreshed in the same approved pass.

stage_on_trigger.rule: On voice intake, job talk, or the visit flow, flag the template at its trigger and open it on the back end ready for data. Fill the structure that already exists. Do not invent a checklist mid-rush.
stage_on_trigger.surface_only_relevant: Never push unneeded templates. No standing docs every visit. No Scope on a pure monitoring day unless the user elects it.
examples: After a moisture walk, stage Moisture Log with the points ready.
Fan moved for a wet-spot shift: stage Equipment - <Room> (and refresh Master) with what moved, why, and how, so positions correlate with later reading changes.
Map or demo cues: stage or update Mitigation Scope - <Room> plus room Source of Loss and Pre-existing Damage as needed.
Plan or hold change: update living Mitigation Scope (order of work and checkboxes) or Hazards / Holds. Do not recreate a Day Forward note.
New layer opened: log it the same day, layer by layer, into Mitigation Scope and into Source of Loss when it is the source. Moisture on a material already in play stages Moisture Log only.

automated_checks.offer_only: Both modes offer or stage. Neither writes Encircle. The user approves any write.
automated_checks.passive: Visit ended: offer the notes for what actually happened. Visit Summary, Moisture Log, and Equipment every visit that earned them. Mitigation Scope, Source of Loss, and Pre-existing Damage only if map or demo cues fired. Hazards / Holds only if a hold changed. Do not offer Day Forward.
automated_checks.photo_timing_rule: HARD RULE on leaving (Encircle Operations: Approach vs Leave Photo Analysis). Offer voice and audio notes for what happened. Do not analyze photos to fill those notes. Today's departure and just-taken photos may not have uploaded to Encircle yet. A missing photo means not uploaded yet, never that the work never happened. Formal photo-backed notes wait until end of day or the next day. Stage and offer only. Never write Encircle from this kit.
automated_checks.note_style_rule: HARD RULE (Encircle Operations: Easy-to-read Note Style). Staged and offered note text stays easy to read. Short sentences, not long paragraphs. A line break between sections. Applies to notes produced with Encircle and RestoKit. Stage and offer only. Never write Encircle from this kit.
automated_checks.active: Upcoming Day-0 inspection: flag it early. Remind upcoming tasks and current tasks. A Day-0 flag includes Inspection as the intake note (Note Templates: Templates inspection), and does not pull standing docs that have not changed.
automated_checks.restokit_tag_rule: HARD RULE (Note Templates: RestoKit Tag Rule). Every scope, note, or template the kit writes uses a plain title with no ◇ prefix (for example 'Mitigation Scope', 'Visit Summary', 'Moisture Log', 'Inspection') and ends with a single footer line: ◇ resto_kit. Do not add a 'made with RestoKit' line or any other tag in the body. Existing notes whose titles still start with ◇ are recognized as the same notes.

materials_fill_path.rule: That skill is the default fill path for Scope, room SOL, and Monitoring. Map materials-by-room and meter readings into those templates. Do not invent Hydro point IDs.
materials_fill_path.note_style_rule: HARD RULE (Encircle Operations: Easy-to-read Note Style). Filled note bodies stay easy to read. Short sentences, not long paragraphs. A line break between sections. Stage and offer only. Never write Encircle.
materials_fill_path.logged: Materials are logged every inspection and every demo, layer by layer as they are opened. A new exposure, such as framing just opened, is entered the same day.
materials_fill_path.moisture: Moisture is logged daily for each material currently in play.
materials_fill_path.triggers: A material or reading trigger stages the matching template here. Monitoring does not start a new materials list by itself.
materials_fill_path.monitoring_materials: Monitoring checks logged-current materials only. No default prompt to add a new material. The user may elect to add one.
materials_fill_path.tramex_wood_timber: Tramex Moisture Encounter Wood/Timber scale max is 30. Needle pegged is MAXED at 30. About 25 is near the ceiling, not mid-range. Do not mix that scale with Tramex Drywall/Plaster.

visit_note_cadence.template_recognition: Kit templates are recognized from Note Templates (plain titles and body headings) and from speech that names the visit, the note, or the work that triggers one. Existing notes whose titles still start with ◇ (the 1.0.1 title form) are the same notes: recognize them. Numbered company pickers (01 through 06b) are aliases for those same notes. Daily-log shape is Daily Log Template, not a visit note.
visit_note_cadence.conflict_log: If speech and a file disagree, use Daily Log Template: Conflict Log. Keep both sides, confirm or correct before commit, and mark only when they differ.
visit_note_cadence.note_style_rule: HARD RULE (Encircle Operations: Easy-to-read Note Style). Staged and offered note text stays easy to read. Short sentences, not long paragraphs. A line break between sections. Applies to notes produced with Encircle and RestoKit. Stage and offer only. Never write Encircle from this kit.
visit_note_cadence.voice_considerations: In a rush, finish the one thing in front of you, then take the staged note that already matches it. Do not hand over a standing plan or a scope sheet that this visit did not earn. That note stays easy to read: short sentences, and a line break between sections (Note Style Rule).
test_intake_lines: Every later visit stages Visit Summary, Moisture Log, and Equipment when that work happened.
A pure monitoring day does not get a new scope note unless you ask for it.
Inspection is Day 0 only. It is in Note Templates.
Nothing here posts to Encircle. Staged notes wait for an explicit yes.
Every note this kit writes uses a plain title and ends with the diamond resto_kit footer. No 'made with' line.
Tramex Wood/Timber pegged is 30, not a mid-scale number. Do not invent a Hydro point ID.
Moisture Log reads materials already logged. It does not ask for a new material unless you elect one.
Staged notes stay easy to read. Short sentences. A line break between sections.
Day Forward is scrapped. What's next lives in living Mitigation Scope notes.
visit_note_cadence.reference_note: Template bodies, plain titles, and the ◇ resto_kit footer rule live in Note Templates. This module says when to stage them.

note_templates.title: Note Templates and Scope Sheets
note_templates.description: The full generic template set the kit stages and writes: Day-0 inspection, visit notes, moisture log, hazards and holds, equipment master and room notes, living mitigation scope (room source plus Master rollup), source of loss, pre-existing damage, job voice data, job-file review questions, and the billable mitigation scope sheet. A company may still keep its own native forms; those are recognized as aliases. When this kit writes a scope, note, or template, it uses the plain titles in this module and ends every output with the ◇ resto_kit footer.

restokit_tag_rule.name: restokit_tag
restokit_tag_rule.stated: Every scope, note, or template the kit writes uses a plain title with no ◇ prefix and ends with a single footer line: ◇ resto_kit. Do not add a 'made with RestoKit' line or any other tag in the body.
restokit_tag_rule.reason: Outputs should read like a natural, fluent person wrote them, super organized but not AI-sounding. The unusual mark sits out of sight at the bottom, which minimizes ego.
restokit_tag_rule.applies_to: Every scope, note, template, or sheet the kit stages or writes.
restokit_tag_rule.plain_titles: The note title is the note name only, with no ◇ prefix. Example: 'Inspection · MM/DD/YY'.
restokit_tag_rule.footer: The last line of every RestoKit output is exactly: ◇ resto_kit
restokit_tag_rule.no_other_tag: Do not add a 'made with RestoKit' line or any other tag in the body.
restokit_tag_rule.legacy_titles: Existing notes whose titles still start with ◇ remain valid. Recognize those old titles as the same notes. New writes use the plain title and the footer. The documentation room is still named ◇ RestoKit so existing files keep their room.

restokit_tag_rule.speakable: Titles stay plain. Every note this kit writes ends with the diamond resto_kit line at the bottom. No 'made with' line.

principles.newest_first: Every accumulative doc or note lists days newest at the top, older below. Applies to Moisture Log visit blocks, scope change history, Visit Summary across visits, and any other note that stacks over time.
principles.blanks_stay_open: Blanks stay open. Never guessed. Values read from a photo are tagged (from photo).
principles.no_blame: No blame in notes. Customer requests are written 'per customer'.
principles.footer: Every RestoKit output ends with a single footer line: ◇ resto_kit. Do not add a 'made with RestoKit' line or any other tag in the body. The unusual mark sits out of sight at the bottom, which minimizes ego.
principles.writing_style: Field labels end with colons, not dashes. Use plain human wording. Use 'gate' only for operational steps and stages (for example Job-Type Gate, Final Verification Gate); elsewhere use plain words like hold or check. Do not use em-dashes as field separators. Outputs should read like a natural, fluent person wrote them: super organized, not AI-sounding.
principles.plain_english: Plain English for techs and adjusters. Short sentences, with a line break between sections (Encircle Operations: Easy-to-read Note Style).
principles.master_sub: Master/sub is locked for Mitigation Scope and Equipment only. The room note is the source; Master is a rollup only, refreshed in the same approved pass. Never edit Master directly.
principles.moisture_and_hazards_are_different_recor: Moisture Log and Hazards / Holds are different records: each is a single note, not master/sub. No Moisture Master, no Hazards Master, and no per-room Moisture or Hazards subs.
principles.source_and_preexisting_are_room_only: Source of Loss and Pre-existing Damage stay room-only (no Master).
principles.day_forward_scrapped: Day Forward is scrapped (11/05/26). 'What's next' (order of work, holds and gates at the top tied to the lines they block, open [] / done [X] / partial [~]) lives in the living Mitigation Scope notes. Do not recreate a Day Forward note. PM office checklist items stay on Visit Summary or the company's PM board, not in Mitigation Scope.
principles.native_forms_may_stay: A company may keep its own native Inspection Template or Daily Production form. Those can be filled from the kit notes. The kit still writes the plain titles and ends every output with the ◇ resto_kit footer.
principles.encircle_boundary: Stage and offer only. This kit never writes Encircle. Drafts wait for an explicit yes. Only the authorized connector writes, and only after the user approves.
principles.restokit_room: Every file the kit documents gets one room named ◇ RestoKit. That room holds Job Voice Data, Moisture Log, Mitigation Scope - Master, and Equipment - Master. Room scopes and room equipment notes go in the actual affected rooms.

moisture_log_rules.where: Single living note in the ◇ RestoKit room. Title: Moisture Log · updated MM/DD/YY. Edit in place. New visit blocks prepend at the top.
moisture_log_rules.line_format: time PT · location · value · material (confirmed/unconfirmed) · flags
moisture_log_rules.image_not_folder: Check the image, not the folder. Photos filed in the wrong room are common. The folder is only a hint. Flag wrong-room shots and never assign readings by folder.
moisture_log_rules.capture_time: Each line is labeled by room and capture time (Pacific). Leave app photo numbers out; they shift when a photo is deleted.
moisture_log_rules.raw_values_only: Never convert between meters or scales. Name the meter and mode in each visit header.
moisture_log_rules.material_labels: confirmed = verified by a voice or field note for that room and reading. unconfirmed = identified from the photo alone. Every reading line gets one of these labels.
moisture_log_rules.exclusions: Metal, duct, and equipment-panel readings are logged in the note but kept off the drying graphs.
moisture_log_rules.graphs: Graphs are made at closeout, not on every update. One image per room, from the note, using the meter's own scale bands. Mixed scales go on separate axes or panels. Suggested filename: Moisture Graph · <Room> · updated MM/DD/YY.png.

equipment_master_rules.where: Rollup only, in the ◇ RestoKit room. Title: Equipment - Master · updated MM/DD/YY. Not edited directly. Refreshed when a room equipment note changes.
equipment_master_rules.line_format: <model or unit name>, <type>[ placement], <date first seen/mentioned MM/DD> (<source>[; photo <capture time> PT])
equipment_master_rules.sources: Use one of: voice, note, photo. Prefer a single source on the line. When a voice confirmation and a photo both confirm the same unit, you may write voice; photo HH:MM AM/PM PT.
rules: One line per unit. Room headers group the lines. No guessed brands or models.
No photo numbers. Use capture time in Pacific (photo 4:42 PM PT).
If the model is unknown, write model TBD. Do not invent a brand or model.
A voice confirmation on site beats photo and notes when they conflict.
Check image content. Photos are often filed in the wrong room. The folder is only a hint.

Type words: dehu for dehumidifiers; AFD for air filtration devices. Do not use HEPA alone as the type word (HEPA is a filter type; model names like HEPA 700 stay as labeled). Negative air is placement on an AFD (AFD on negative air).
Notes section for non-unit items (spider box power path and similar).
Still need line at the bottom for serials, unknown models, unconfirmed pulls, and air-mover totals.

job_file_review.title: Job file review
job_file_review.when: Run these eleven questions every time before building or updating Mitigation Scope: a new intake, a catch-up job, or a morning meeting. Day Forward is scrapped.
job_file_review.style: Keep answers short and plain. Don't invent facts. Don't over-engineer. Every action that later becomes a checkbox should support a billable line. Into-file note after the meeting is delta only.
questions: What's the source, category, and class, and what still isn't confirmed?
Where has water moved since the last visit (rooms, wicking, crawl/underside)? What's preliminary vs mapped?
What's on hold (asbestos, lead, gas, HVAC, structural)? What can't be disturbed until what clears?
Contents / access: what has to move or pack out before work, and who owns that cost?
For each demo or "save" call: what's the billable path, and what's the second-order hit (materials, customer, extra damage, rework)?
Cabinets / finishes: cut-for-sample vs remove. Which is cheaper once you price the damage and the restore?
Floor layers: remove to where, pause at what suspect material, photo/reading proof for the claim?
Containment and negative air: where's the line, why there, and does equipment/power support it?
Equipment on site: what's running, what's still needed, dehu size vs chamber, labels/serials for the file?
Customer / house: age, pets, occupancy, access windows. Anything that changes the sequence?
Every checkbox you're about to write: which line item or billable unit does it support? Drop or reword anything that doesn't.
output_that_feeds_mitigation_scope: What must clear before work starts
Open holds and who owns them
Next concrete work order (holds first, then lines)
Job-wide lines parked on a home room
job_file_review.if_written_as_a_note: If this review is written into the file, title it Job File Review · MM/DD/YY. Prefer a short talk and then update the living scope notes.

billable_mitigation.title: Mitigation Scope Sheet (billable)
billable_mitigation.description: Generic billable mitigation labor sheet, transcribed from a third-party industry scope sheet (rev 10.16.17) as a baseline of commonly billed mitigation work, plus kit gap lines G1–G20 in execution order. This is a working draft, not a finished company form. It may contain reading errors from the source photos.

## Transcription notes (remove before printing)

- **1**: Option codes LS and LF are not defined on the sheet. Best guess: LS = lead sample/swab taken; LF = lead-free (or lead result filed); A = asbestos tested; N/A = not required. Confirm with source or replace with plain choices.
- **65**: Cat 3 marker sits between rows 64 and 65 because the photo is skewed. Best guess: Row 65 (pressure wash / under sill plates / extract). The row is shaded like other Cat 3 rows and the text slope places the marker there. Row 64 (clean joists) not flagged.
- **85**: Cat 3 column shows '#' rather than '3'. Best guess: Count marker (enter number of power boxes), not a Cat 3 flag. Treated cat3_flag=false.
- **82**: ETES: electric thermal energy system (confirmed by Jason 2026-11-12); written out in the kit, no acronym.
- **room cell 'A' marker**: Most room cells print a small checkbox at left and a letter 'A' at right; meaning not stated. Best guess: 'A' = all (entire room) shortcut instead of a measured quantity; the checkbox appears mainly on Cat 3 rows and may mean 'performed under Cat 3 conditions'. Not modeled per cell; confirm.
- **17, 43, 45, 59, 67, 69**: No unit printed. Best guess: 17 SF, 43 SF, 45 SF, 59 EA, 67 SF or HRS, 69 SF or HRS.

daily_log_template._note: Embedded copy of logs/daily_log_template_v0.2.json. Use when the user starts, adds to, or closes a daily log. The logs/ file stays the v0.2 schema. Kit copy adds voice-to-tiers fill, template recognition, and the conflict log. v0.2 remains the active daily object.

instructions.voice: Write entries as close to verbatim as possible to how they were spoken. Preserve phrasing, word choice, and order. Only remove filler: 'ums', stutters, false starts, repeated words, typos. Do not paraphrase, summarize, or tidy the meaning. If cleaning changes what was meant, it is too much. A reader should hear the speaker's voice, not a cleaned-up version of it.

when_to_push: Between job sites: natural break, fresh context, low error rate
Lunch: midday checkpoint, catches the morning's drift
End of day: final sweep, not the only write
when_not_to_push: Raw or emotional entries written in the moment: let them sit, edit at the next gate
push_policy.gate: Before any push, read back the diff in one line. Confirm or decline. Nothing pushes without explicit yes.
push_policy.note: Repo is private forever. Tier 3 (human) pushes with tiers 1 and 2 at every gate. No private shelf.

tiers.tier1_material: Objective, countable, billable. Square footage, stairs, category, dwell time, equipment moved, hours on site, arrival, departure, address. No interpretation.
tiers.tier2_decisions: Socialized technical calls. Questions asked, answers given, outcomes, work_changed flag. If it changed the work, it goes here.
tiers.tier3_human: Interactions, tone, friction, warmth, rank plays. If it changed how you felt about the work, it goes here. Same event can land in tier 2 and tier 3. Employee references by first name only. Customer-identifying detail allowed. No direct customer quotes: paraphrase the exchange, keep the names and the dynamic.

timesheet_fields.note: Mirror the company daily time sheet exactly so one entry feeds both the company records and the signed paper.

No more than 2 stops at the shop without manager approval

daily_log_template.lunch_rule: Lunch is recorded to the actual minute, not a flat 30.

voice_to_tiers_and_timesheet.rule: Spoken day-log talk fills the v0.2 entry. The record stays near-verbatim (Daily Log Template: Instructions: Voice): strip filler only, do not paraphrase meaning. The same talk is sorted into tiers and the timesheet.
voice_to_tiers_and_timesheet.tier1_material: Countable, billable facts land in tier1_material as spoken: square footage, stairs, category, dwell, equipment moved, hours, arrival, departure, address. No interpretation.
voice_to_tiers_and_timesheet.tier2_decisions: A call that changed the work lands in tier2_decisions: question, answer, outcome, and work_changed. If it changed the work, it goes here.
voice_to_tiers_and_timesheet.tier3_human: Tone, friction, warmth, and rank plays land in tier3_human. Employees by first name only. Paraphrase customers. No direct customer quotes. The same event can sit in tier 2 and tier 3.
voice_to_tiers_and_timesheet.timesheet: clock_in and clock_out stay top-level. Timesheet rows mirror the paper: address_or_lunch, time_in, time_out, notes, shop_time_initials. Totals are reg_time_total and after_hours_total. Lunch is the actual minute (lunch_rule), not a flat 30. Shop time over 45 minutes in a day needs manager initials. More than 2 shop stops in a day needs manager approval.
voice_to_tiers_and_timesheet.push_gates: Between sites, lunch, and end of day. Read the diff back in one line. Nothing pushes without an explicit yes. Tier 3 rides with tiers 1 and 2 at every gate. Do not push mid-task.

template_recognition.rule: Recognize a template from the file's contents and from speech.
template_recognition.daily_log: A file that carries the v0.2 entry shape (clock_in, clock_out, timesheet, tier1_material, tier2_decisions, tier3_human) is this daily log, even if the filename differs. Speech that starts a day, names a clock time, adds a tier, or closes the day is the same object.
template_recognition.visit_notes: Visit notes are recognized from plain titles and body headings in Note Templates, from existing notes whose titles still start with ◇ (the 1.0.1 title form), from numbered company pickers 01 through 06b (aliases), and from speech that names the visit or the work that triggers one. They stage through Visit Note Cadence. They are not daily-log tiers.

conflict_log.rule: When voice and a file disagree, keep a lightweight conflict log with both sides. Confirm or correct before commit. Mark a conflict only when the two sides differ. Leave clean files unmarked.
conflict_log.applies_to: Daily-log fields, and a visit-note file when spoken facts contradict what is already on disk. Same rule either way.
conflict_log.commit: Do not commit either side until the user confirms or corrects. After resolution, write the chosen side. Drop the mark when nothing else conflicts.

encircle_operations.purpose: How to work Encircle job files with the user: pull, evaluate, read photos, and prepare entries for review.
rules: Only the authorized Encircle connector holds the Encircle API token, read-only. All other access goes through that connector.
Encircle is read-only. Nothing is written or sent to Encircle without the user's explicit OK each time. Placement notes and labels are drafts until the user says go.
Pull one job file at a time, on request. Evaluate it, then talk it through with the user and agree on the plan.
Cached customer data for a job is wiped when the job closes. Callbacks re-pull from Encircle. Local daily logs are the company's own records.
Policyholder phone, email and policy number stay with the authorized Encircle connector unless the user approves.
Encircle job data is never stored in this kit file. Only the method lives here.

HARD RULE: Approach vs Leave Photo Analysis. The reason is attached on that object. On approach, photo analysis of photos already in the file is OK for homework and file prep. On leaving, do not use photos for analysis to enter notes: today's departure and just-taken photos may not have uploaded yet. A missing photo means not uploaded yet, never that the work never happened. Formal photo-backed notes wait until end of day or the next day. Voice and audio notes during the visit are still OK. Stage and offer only. Never write Encircle from this kit.

HARD RULE: Photo Evidence Limits (AI photo readings). The reason is attached on that object. Photo reads are limited to reliable identifications: room, equipment, objects, and containment. A photo of a moisture meter's display is an allowed reading (label non-wood modes as comparative, not %MC). Material and location behind a meter-reading photo are confirmed by a voice note on the same clock whose content matches; timestamp proximity alone does not confirm. Appearance-based calls (moisture, wicking, stains, shadows, textures, finishes, material type, condition) stay unverified until a meter or a person confirms them, and must not propagate into decisions, scopes, billables, or drying conclusions. Full text: Encircle Operations: Photo Evidence Limits, including Bulk Confirmation of Meter-reading Photos When no audio was recorded with the photos, point the user to the wettest reading per material per room to confirm by voice or tap; the rest stay unconfirmed (U) but stay backed by their photos. Photo analysis is limited to what it does well: equipment, meter displays, room identity, and general progression; everything else is reviewed by a person, not trusted 100%.
