HARD RULE: Easy-to-read Note Style (easy-to-read notes). The reason is attached on that object. Notes written with Encircle and RestoKit stay easy to read and concise: short sentences, not long paragraphs, with a line break between sections. Applies to staged and offered note text. Stage and offer only. Never write Encircle from this kit.

HARD RULE: Job Voice Data Line Time. Every line carries the Pacific time, to the minute, when it was said or sent, not the write time, so it matches photo capture times. Full text: Encircle Operations: Job Voice Data Line Time.

HARD RULE: RestoKit tag rule (plain titles, ◇ resto_kit footer). Every scope, note, or template the kit writes uses a plain title with no ◇ prefix (for example 'Mitigation Scope', 'Visit Summary', 'Moisture Log', 'Inspection') and ends with a single footer line: ◇ resto_kit. Do not add a 'made with RestoKit' line or any other tag in the body. Existing notes whose titles still start with ◇ are recognized as the same notes. Full text: Note Templates: RestoKit Tag Rule.

photo_timing_rule.name: Approach vs leave photo analysis
photo_timing_rule.reason: Today's departure photos and photos just taken may not have uploaded to Encircle yet. A photo that is not in the file yet was not uploaded yet. It is not evidence the work never happened.
photo_timing_rule.approach: On approach to a job site, photo analysis for homework and file prep is OK. Use the photos already in the file.
photo_timing_rule.leave: On leaving a job site, do not use photos for analysis to enter notes.
photo_timing_rule.missing_photos: Treat a missing photo as "not uploaded yet," never as "never happened." Do not conclude "no cap was put on" because no photo of the cap is visible yet.
photo_timing_rule.photo_backed_notes: Formal photo-backed notes wait until end of day or the next day, after uploads catch up.
photo_timing_rule.voice_and_audio: Voice and audio notes can still be captured during the visit. They are not blocked. The ban is only photo-based analysis for writing notes at departure.
photo_timing_rule.preexisting_photos_unchanged: The arrival and capture preexisting-damage rule stays: any photo from the initial arrival and capture set can serve as a preexisting-damage photo. It does not need a preexisting-damage label. It is the state of the home at that time.
photo_timing_rule.encircle_boundary: Stage and offer only. This kit never writes Encircle. Placement notes and labels stay drafts until the user says go.
photo_timing_rule.speakable: On the way in, photos already in the file are fair game. On the way out, don't write notes off photos. They may not be up yet. No photo does not mean it didn't happen. Voice notes are fine. Photo notes wait until tonight or tomorrow.

note_style_rule.name: Easy-to-read note style
note_style_rule.reason: Notes written with Encircle and RestoKit have to be easy to read on a phone in the field. A long paragraph gets skipped. Short sentences and a line break between sections keep the note usable.
note_style_rule.easy_to_read: Write the note so a tech can scan it. Plain words. No dense blocks.
note_style_rule.line_breaks: Put a line break between sections.
note_style_rule.applies_to: Notes produced with Encircle and RestoKit. That includes staged and offered note text from this kit and from the company pack. The same style when a staged note is the body the user will paste.
note_style_rule.scope: Note body text. Chat photo tables stay on Output Format Rule.
note_style_rule.encircle_boundary: Stage and offer only. This kit never writes Encircle. Placement notes and labels stay drafts until the user says go.
note_style_rule.speakable: Notes stay easy to read. Short sentences. A line break between sections. We stage the note. We do not write Encircle.

job_voice_data.name: Job Voice Data line time
job_voice_data.rule: Every line in Job Voice Data carries the Pacific time, to the minute, when it was said or sent. Use that time, not the write time, so the line matches photo capture times.
job_voice_data.clock: when it was said or sent
job_voice_data.why: So each line matches photo capture times.
job_voice_data.speakable: On Job Voice Data, every line gets the Pacific time to the minute when it was said or sent. Not when you wrote it down. That's how it lines up with the photos.

note_cadence_alignment.rule: Cadence follows Note Templates and Visit Note Cadence. Day 0 must: Inspection, Job Voice Data, Mitigation Scope - <Room> + Master, Moisture Log, Equipment - <Room> + Master, Visit Summary. Every later visit: Visit Summary, Moisture Log, and Equipment when gear is placed, pulled, counted, or only repositioned. Hazards / Holds only when a hold changes. Map or demo updates living room scopes plus Source of Loss and Pre-existing Damage as needed. Day Forward is scrapped. Every kit-written title is plain, with no ◇ prefix, and every output ends with the ◇ resto_kit footer (Note Templates: RestoKit Tag Rule). Stage and offer only. No Encircle write from this kit.
note_cadence_alignment.note_style_rule: HARD RULE. Full text: Encircle Operations: Easy-to-read Note Style. Staged and offered note text stays easy to read. Short sentences, not long paragraphs. A line break between sections. Stage and offer only. Never write Encircle from this kit.
note_cadence_alignment.preexisting_photos: Unchanged: any photo from the initial arrival and capture set can serve as a preexisting-damage photo. It does not need a preexisting-damage label. It is the state of the home at that time.
note_cadence_alignment.restokit_tag_rule: HARD RULE (Note Templates: RestoKit Tag Rule). Every scope, note, or template the kit writes uses a plain title with no ◇ prefix (for example 'Mitigation Scope', 'Visit Summary', 'Moisture Log', 'Inspection') and ends with a single footer line: ◇ resto_kit. Do not add a 'made with RestoKit' line or any other tag in the body. Existing notes whose titles still start with ◇ are recognized as the same notes.

photo_reading_method: Files are often survey-only, with no logged readings. Readings get taken from photos that show the meter on the material, grouped by room.

For each photo, record the room, the spot, the material, the value, the meter and mode, the photo time, and a confidence for both the value and the material. Material ID from photos can be wrong, so the user corrects it.
Any photo from the initial arrival and capture set can serve as a preexisting-damage photo. It does not need a preexisting-damage label: it is simply the state of the home at that time.
A pinless meter in wood mode gives true %MC only on wood. On LVP or tile the number is only relative to other spots.
Ask the user which photo is the dry standard. Same material throughout means one dry standard covers it.
Ask about photos taken for other reasons, like a customer-requested check of an old loss. Don't count them as part of this loss or as a dry standard.
Sort readings three ways: enter as-is, enter after the user confirms, and leave out (unreadable or unrelated).

Before, after and overview shots with no meter are deliberate: they record the state of things before work (pre-existing condition, contents, finishes). The Subject column can say 'Overview / before state' when that helps, but no special label is required for preexisting damage; every arrival/capture shot already records the home's state. Don't treat them as filler.

Fuzzy reads for blurry dials: place the spot from the layout and neighboring shots by time, crop and zoom the dial, and report the color zone (green, yellow or red) and rough needle position instead of a number. Mark these as zone-only. If neither the needle nor the zone shows, say so and ask the user.

Subject wording: 'floor' means the floor assembly, so always name the layer: finished floor (e.g. LVP), underlayment or subfloor. A pinless reading through LVP may include the layers below. Cabinet parts are named as cabinet parts (cabinet base or bottom panel, toe kick, side panel, interior), never as floor.

Water migrates down through the seams in every layer (LVP joints, underlayment seams, subfloor sheet seams) and out the bottom. Wet readings at the top layer mean check underneath (subfloor and crawlspace) too.
A pinless reading taken against metal (a duct, a pipe, a nail) is probably a false high. Flag it and don't count it.
Don't name a utility from a photo. A pipe is 'likely gas' until someone on site confirms it.
Do not invent Encircle Hydro point IDs. A needle read from a photo stays a photo read until someone logs it as a Hydro point.

HARD RULE (Photo Evidence Limits): AI photo readings are limited to what can be identified reliably: room identity; equipment presence, type, count, and placement (for example AFD vs dehumidifier, and model when the label is visible); objects present; and containment or poly present. Do not treat appearance, moisture, wicking, staining, shadows (a shadow under a cabinet or countertop can look like wicking), textures, finishes, material type, or condition, as evidence for decisions, scopes, billables, or drying conclusions. Log those only as 'unverified observation: needs meter reading or human confirmation', and confirm them with a meter reading or a person before use. A photo of a moisture meter's display is an allowed photo reading: the number and mode on the screen are reliably readable; label non-wood modes as comparative, not %MC. The material and location behind a meter-reading photo are confirmed by a voice note on the same clock (the tech speaks the room, surface or material, and reading while shooting). A material named in a voice note for that room and reading counts as confirmed; a material seen only in a photo stays unconfirmed. Timestamp proximity suggests a link but does not by itself confirm: the voice content has to match (room and material, and the reading if spoken). That lets a whole room's readings be confirmed in one pass without extra taps. Appearance-only readings still never confirm moisture. See Encircle Operations: Photo Evidence Limits, including Meter in Photo and Bulk Confirmation of Meter-reading Photos, and Job Voice Data Line Time, Scope: Living Scope Notes: Evidence Labels, and Technology: Topics: Photo ↔ Audio ↔ Text ↔ Moisture Sync When no audio was recorded with the photos, pick the wettest reading per material per room from meter-display photos and point the user to that photo number to confirm by voice or tap. Once those key readings are confirmed, the rest stay unconfirmed (U) but remain backed by their original photos, which can be checked any time a line is questioned. Optional full pass: a fast review screen shows each photo next to its reading and status for click-through confirmation. Photo analysis is limited to what it does well: equipment, meter displays, room identity, and general progression. Everything else is reviewed by a person, not trusted 100%. See Photo Analysis Scope and Priority Confirmation When No Audio Was Recorded.

HARD RULE (Approach vs Leave Photo Analysis): On approach, read photos already in the file for homework and file prep. On leaving, do not analyze photos to write notes. Today's departure and just-taken photos may not have uploaded yet. A missing photo means not uploaded yet, never that the work never happened. Formal photo-backed notes wait until end of day or the next day. Voice and audio notes during the visit are still OK. The arrival and capture preexisting-damage rule above is unchanged.

photo_evidence_limits.name: Photo evidence limits
photo_evidence_limits.reason: Appearance in a photo can be deceiving. A shadow under a cabinet or countertop can look like wicking. Textures, finishes, stains, and material type are easy to misread.
photo_evidence_limits.allowed: AI photo readings are limited to what can be identified reliably: room identity; equipment presence, type, count, and placement (for example AFD vs dehumidifier, and model when the label is visible); objects present; and containment or poly present. A photo of a moisture meter's display is also allowed: see Meter in Photo and Bulk Confirmation of Meter-reading Photos.
photo_evidence_limits.forbidden_propagation: Appearance-based readings, moisture, wicking, staining, shadows (including a shadow under a cabinet or countertop mistaken for wicking), textures, finishes, material type, and condition, must not propagate into decisions, scopes, billables, or drying conclusions. Log them only as 'unverified observation: needs meter reading or human confirmation'. Confirm with a meter reading or a person before use.
photo_evidence_limits.meter_in_photo: A photo of a moisture meter's display is an allowed photo reading: the number and mode on the screen are reliably readable. Label non-wood modes as comparative, not %MC (see Photo Reading Method and Meter Models). A readable meter display is a meter reading, not an appearance-based call.
photo_evidence_limits.speakable: Photos are good for rooms, gear, objects, and containment. Don't call moisture, wicking, stains, shadows, textures, finishes, or material type from how it looks. Log those as unverified until a meter or a person confirms. Don't let them into decisions, scopes, billables, or drying conclusions. A photo of the meter's screen is a real reading: label non-wood modes as comparative, not percent MC. Confirm the material and spot with a voice note on the same clock, like 'kitchen, north wall drywall, 22'. Close times suggest a link, but the words have to match. That way a whole room can be confirmed in one pass, no extra taps. If no audio was recorded with the photos, start with the wettest reading per material per room: point the user at that photo number to confirm by voice or tap. Once those key readings are confirmed, the rest stay unconfirmed but stay backed by their photos, so a questioned line can be checked. There's an optional fast review screen to click through the rest. Photo analysis is only trusted for what it does well: equipment, meter displays, room identity, and general progression. Everything else is reviewed by a person. Don't put full trust in it. A wall that just looks wet still doesn't count.

bulk_confirmation.name: Bulk confirmation of meter-reading photos
bulk_confirmation.material_and_location: The material and location behind a meter-reading photo are confirmed by a voice note on the same clock. The tech speaks the room, the surface or material, and the reading while shooting: for example 'kitchen, north wall drywall, 22'. A material named in a voice note for that room and reading counts as confirmed. A material seen only in a photo stays unconfirmed. This is the (C) confirmed / (U) unconfirmed material label: see Scope: Living Scope Notes: Evidence Labels.
bulk_confirmation.timestamp_proximity: Timestamp proximity between a photo and audio suggests a link but does not by itself confirm. Confirmation needs the voice content to match: room and material, and the reading if it was spoken. Use the spoken-time clock in Encircle Operations: Job Voice Data Line Time (gathered in Scope: Living Scope Notes: Voice Timestamps), not the write time, so voice lines line up with photo capture times. Photo-to-audio lining-up is described in Technology: Topics: Photo ↔ Audio ↔ Text ↔ Moisture Sync.
bulk_confirmation.one_pass: This lets a whole room's readings be confirmed in one pass without extra taps.
bulk_confirmation.appearance_never_confirms: Appearance-only readings (a wall that looks wet, shadows, staining) still never confirm moisture.

photo_evidence_limits.photo_analysis_scope: Photo analysis is limited to what it does well: equipment, meter displays, room identity, and general progression. Everything else is reviewed by a person, not trusted 100%.

priority_confirmation.name: Priority confirmation when no audio was recorded
priority_confirmation.when: Use this path when no audio was recorded with the photos.
priority_confirmation.wettest_first: The AI picks the wettest reading per material per room from meter-display photos and points the user to that photo number to confirm, by voice or by tap.
priority_confirmation.rest_stay_unconfirmed: Once the key (wettest) readings are confirmed, the rest stay labeled unconfirmed (U) but remain backed by their original photos, which can be checked any time a line is questioned.
priority_confirmation.optional_full_pass: Optional full pass: a fast review screen shows each photo next to its reading and confirmed/unconfirmed status for click-through confirmation.

must_do_reminders: PRINT THE PHOTO MAP TABLE: The user may not see photo numbers the same way in Encircle on a tablet. Always deliver a plain-text README table of photo number, Encircle timestamp (PT) and room, no images or PDF, so the user can match photos in the app.
Note the photo times in Pacific time, down to the second.
Job Voice Data: every line carries the Pacific time, to the minute, when it was said or sent (not the write time), so it matches photo capture times (Job Voice Data Line Time).
Flag a missing work authorization, crawlspace, atmospheric readings, equipment, and a missing cause of loss or rooms.
Keep it honest: entries made from survey photos are labeled as taken from photos, not logged live. Label wording for those entries is an open decision.
Plain titles on every kit-written note (Note Templates: RestoKit Tag Rule). End every output with a single footer line: ◇ resto_kit. No 'made with' line.
open_decisions: The label wording for readings taken from photos when they're entered into Encircle.
encircle_operations.output_format_rule: When working job files with the user, always output in chat as plain-text markdown tables, one separate table per room (sorted by room): photo number, Encircle timestamp in PT, room, subject matter (what the photo shows: material and spot), reading if any, and a Question/Note column (chat only, never in Encircle labels) for a question or flag on that photo (blank if none). Never PDFs, contact sheets or image collages unless the user asks.

confidence_scale.Confirmed: Read or confirmed by the tech on site. Humans beat photo reads; a tech's value overrides mine.
confidence_scale.High: Needle and scale clear, or needle clear with soft numbers. Value within about ±1-2. Treat as a real reading.
confidence_scale.Medium: Needle visible but blurred, small, angled or glared. Range about 4 points. Usually right; good enough to map wet and dry.
confidence_scale.Low: Color zone only. Use the middle value of that meter model's zone (see Meter Models), shifted toward a neighboring zone if the needle sits near it.
confidence_scale.Inferred: Nothing readable. Value filled in from neighboring readings and layout. Never entered as measured.
confidence_scale.calibration_note: Photo reads have held up against the tech's own memory (e.g. photo 35: zone read red, tech confirmed ~22). Don't undersell clear reads; still defer to the tech on anything he remembers.

fields: Meter and mode: only on the first photo in the file where that meter appears (later photos assume the same meter unless it changes; note again when a different meter shows up)

Basis: a short plain description of how the value was read and why it's that certain (e.g. 'needle and scale clear', 'needle visible, numbers blurred', 'color only, mid-zone value', 'glare, inferred from neighbor at 27', 'confirmed by tech on site')
encircle_photo_label_format.exclude: No questions in Encircle labels. Questions stay in chat with the user.
encircle_photo_label_format.example: 4:09:11 PM | LVP at sink-run toe kick corner | ~24-25 | Tramex Encounter Plus, pinless, wood mode | Needle and scale clear (first meter photo); later labels drop the meter field
encircle_photo_label_format.note: No confidence labels in Encircle. The basis description replaces them. The Confidence Scale stays as internal guidance for wording the basis.

meter_models.note: Color-zone values and scales are model-specific. Add each new model here before using zone reads with it.

tramex_moisture_encounter_plus.notes: True %MC only on wood; relative on LVP and tile. Wood/Timber scale max is 30. Pegged right is MAXED at 30. Mid-20s are near the ceiling, not mid-range. Do not mix this scale with Tramex Drywall/Plaster. Do not invent Hydro point IDs.

On approach, photo analysis of photos already in the file is OK for this review. On leaving, do not fill notes from photo analysis: today's departure and just-taken shots may not have uploaded. A room or a step with no photo means not uploaded yet, not that the work never happened. Formal photo-backed notes wait until end of day or the next day. Voice and audio notes from the visit are still OK. Arrival and capture photos remain valid preexisting-damage photos. Stage and offer only. Never write Encircle from this kit.

AI photo readings are limited to reliable identifications: room identity, equipment presence/type/count/placement, objects present, and containment or poly. A photo of a moisture meter's display is an allowed reading: the number and mode on the screen are reliably readable; label non-wood modes as comparative, not %MC. Confirm the material and location behind a meter-reading photo with a voice note on the same clock whose content matches (room and material, and the reading if spoken); timestamp proximity alone does not confirm. That lets a whole room's readings be confirmed in one pass without extra taps. Appearance-based readings (moisture, wicking, staining, shadows, textures, finishes, material type, condition) must not propagate into decisions, scopes, billables, or drying conclusions, and appearance-only readings still never confirm moisture. job_file_review_workflow.template: Use the company's job-file review template if they have one.
job_file_review_workflow.morning_use: Run this before any day-forward plan. Same questions for a new intake, a catch-up job, and a morning meeting. Pull Encircle read-only, then walk the questions with the person and RestoKit. Short plain answers. Don't invent. Don't over-engineer. The person's word beats a photo guess. Every later checkbox must support a billable line. Second-order effects (job, materials, customer, rework) get a hard look. Full text stays in the company's template, if they have one. After the review, the day-forward plan uses the company's day-forward template if they have one.
job_file_review_workflow.morning_note_delta: After the morning meeting, the into-file note is delta only. Full rule: Encircle Operations: Job File Review Workflow: Day Forward Plan: Morning Note. Decisions made, work to do today, who's assigned, holds or gates that changed. Do not reprint cause, Cat, rooms, meters, or gear already in the file. Lands in concrete Day N+1 and/or a thin visit instruction. Do not dump it into 01, 03, or 04 as if new.
questions: What's the source, category, and class, and what still isn't confirmed?
Where has water moved since the last visit (rooms, wicking, crawl/underside)? What's preliminary vs mapped?
What's on hold (asbestos, lead, gas, HVAC, structural)? What can't be disturbed until what clears?
Contents / access: what has to move or pack out before work, and who owns that cost?
For each demo or "save" call: what's the billable path, and what's the second-order hit (materials, customer, extra damage, rework)?
Cabinets / finishes: cut-for-sample vs remove, which is cheaper once you price the damage and the restore?
Floor layers: remove to where, pause at what suspect material, photo/reading proof for the claim?
Containment and negative air: where's the line, why there, and does equipment/power support it?
Equipment on site: what's running, what's still needed, dehu size vs chamber, labels/serials for the file?
Customer / house: age, pets, occupancy, access windows; anything that changes the sequence?
Every checkbox you're about to write: which line item or billable unit does it support? Drop or reword anything that doesn't.
steps: 1. Pull the job: photos, floor plan or sketch, notes, readings. Read-only.
2. Build the per-room photo table: photo number, timestamp (PT), room, subject, reading, Question/Note.
3. Walk the eleven questions in the company's job-file review template, if they have one. Same list for a new intake, a catch-up job, and a morning meeting. Ask, don't assume.
4. Fold in the person's answers. The person's word beats a photo guess. Drop items they rule out; keep true unknowns marked unknown. Short plain answers. Don't invent. Don't over-engineer.
5. Produce the deliverables below. The day-forward plan comes after this review, using the company's day-forward template if they have one.
deliverables: Already done: work completed so far, with amounts (e.g. extraction SF, source fixed).
Billable completed table: item, measurement, confidence, basis.
Day-forward plan, after this review, using the company's day-forward template if they have one. Lead reminder first, then role checklists PM, then Lead, then Techs.
Floor covering estimate: photos against the floor plan, low, likely and high, with a calibration log.
job_file_review_workflow.photo_reference_rule: Office, review and billing docs cite photos as '#N (time, Room)'. To-do checklists never use photo numbers or timestamps. Techs won't look them up. Say in plain words what to photograph or which thing you mean, like 'the china cabinet by the dining-side door'.
pm_rules: PM checklist lines are office work only: scheduling, calls, coordination. That says who owns the line. The person is still a technician. See Leadership and Labor: PM on Site.
Subcontracted work is worded 'Schedule ...'. The PM schedules it; he doesn't do it.
Schedule the asbestos survey before demo. The testing company does the sampling. The state requires it regardless of house age.

If a sample spot sits behind cabinets, plan access: a cut through the cabinet back, a pilot hole, or a second test visit after the cabinets come out. A second visit gets scheduled before that wall is demoed.
Schedule contents: moves, pack-out and inventory go to the contents sub. Big or fragile furniture in the way of containment gets scheduled right away.
Schedule a licensed gas disconnect only for gas appliances that actually have to move.
Cabinet keep-or-replace calls get made in the office once the toe kick findings are in.
tech_rules: Don't disturb suspect materials until the survey clears.
First thing next visit, photograph the inside of every cabinet, doors open, for the contents crew.
Pull toe kicks to see how the cabinets are set and what floor runs under them.
Appliances out first, then work top-down.
Stone countertops can often be saved. Detach them, carry them on edge, and store them out of the work area.
Check whether the backsplash sits on the countertop. The bottom row may have to come out first.
Clear all fasteners from the flooring.

Wall cavities: no cavity dryers for now. Cut one bay open, big enough for your head and shoulders, and meter from the top side. Reach a chase from the work side, not the finished face of the next room.
Crawlspace: poly tent with the dehu inside. Meter the underside of the ducts and the duct wrap when the boots show leaking.
Before cutting, check clearance behind and below the cut (normal high interior caution).
HVAC in the water path: keep the system off or the register sealed. Inspect the boot and the run, by camera if you can.
Wet duct insulation: photo it, flag it, bag it if it's saturated.
Crawl: log the insulation square footage and the bag count, pull pooled water, and note the vapor barrier damage. If the HVAC is in the way, work it out with the lead, PM by phone.
Readings and a photo of each layer as it's exposed, tape measure in frame.
Fast leak: the wettest spot keeps moving. Hunt it every visit.
Plumbing disconnect: sink supply and drain, P-trap, cap the lines, disposal, dishwasher drain and supply.
Containment goes far enough that the wet floor is inside. Add a zipper door for access.
Furniture in the way: let the contents crew empty it. Scoot it on sliders or pads, never drag it on a finished floor.
Stone tops: score the caulk or grout first. Use enough hands, carry on edge, support the sink cutout. If they're stored outside, keep them covered and off the ground.
Blurry meter photo: retake it in focus with the screen readable.
Mark wet edges with blue tape 6 inches to a foot past the last reading, fuzz included (Initial Assessment: Moisture Mapping Tape Line).
cat1_fast_break_equipment: Clean, fast break: no HEPA before demo.
During demo, run the HEPA on negative pressure, ducted outside.
After demo, take the HEPA off the outside ducting and leave it running inside the containment (static pressure).
Air movers only once materials are exposed.
Size equipment by the unit type and rated CFM, the manufacturer guidance, and the readings. Do not invent pint or CFM ratios. The crawl gets its own unit.

scope.description: Existing scope text gathered here, wording unchanged from each source. Original source sections keep that text and point here with gathered_in.

kit_scope.text: Restoration technical execution. Not legal advice, not medical advice, not an insurance-coverage opinion.

outside_scope.text: Assessing indoor contamination (IEP work), regulated materials (asbestos, lead, silica, mercury, PCBs, pesticides, fuels, solvents, radiological), and bird/bat-dropping pathogens are outside the water and mold standards.

scope_note.text: Pre-equipment screen only. Capture room RH before equipment is placed so the impact shows. After equipment is placed, switch to GPP-first psychrometry: do not use starting RH as the primary drying performance metric.

text.rule: Visible damage is rarely the full extent. Plan on the scope growing as you chase water into hidden pathways.
text.voice_note: Initial visual scope is almost always low. The water has usually been busy while you weren't looking.

phase0_principle.text: The surveyor does not lock scope. Initial scopes are almost always low: water hides behind baseplates, in interstitial spaces, and under flooring you can't read through. The file carries the assumption that scope grows.

text.description: The common practice of progressively discovering and adjusting scope as hidden water is revealed during demo and investigation.
common_hidden_paths: Along the backside of baseplates and bottom plates
Interstitial spaces (wall cavities, behind cabinets, under toe kicks, inside vanities)
Under vapor-barrier flooring (LVP, hardwood over slab, tile)
Behind trim, baseboards, and quarter round
Into checks, end grain, and voids in wood framing
text.field_reality: On many jobs, especially Category 2/3 or with significant dwell time, you will need to expand the original scope as you chase water into hidden areas. This is normal and expected.
text.approach: Start with the known wet areas. As you demo, actively look for and follow water into hidden spaces. Continue expanding until you stop finding active moisture or water staining. Document the progression.
text.mindset: Be prepared for scope to grow during the job. 'Chasing the water' is part of doing the job correctly, not scope creep.
text.voice_note: Initial scopes are almost always low on these jobs. Water hides behind baseplates, in interstitial spaces, and under flooring you can't read through. Keep opening things up until you stop finding wet material.

survey_investigation.description: Walk the affected areas and mark where the water is: visible wet, staining, and suspected hidden paths. Marking is rough; the tech on site sets exact readings and containment from it. Make the first category call and write down why. Flag suspect materials; building age raises the bar but doesn't clear anything.
survey_investigation.voice_line: Walking it now: marking visible wet, stains, and where it probably went that we can't see. First category call goes in the file with the reason.

text: What's the source, category, and class, and what still isn't confirmed?
Where has water moved since the last visit (rooms, wicking, crawl/underside)? What's preliminary vs mapped?

photo_evidence_limits.text: AI photo readings are limited to reliable identifications: room identity; equipment presence, type, count, and placement; objects present; and containment or poly present. A photo of a moisture meter's display is an allowed reading: the number and mode on the screen are reliably readable; label non-wood modes as comparative, not %MC. The material and location behind a meter-reading photo are confirmed by a voice note on the same clock whose content matches; a material named in a voice note for that room and reading counts as confirmed, and a material seen only in a photo stays unconfirmed. Timestamp proximity suggests a link but does not by itself confirm. This lets a whole room's readings be confirmed in one pass without extra taps. Appearance-based readings, moisture, wicking, staining, shadows (including a shadow under a cabinet or countertop mistaken for wicking), textures, finishes, material type, and condition, must not propagate into decisions, scopes, billables, or drying conclusions, and appearance-only readings still never confirm moisture. Log them only as 'unverified observation: needs meter reading or human confirmation', and confirm with a meter reading or a person before use When no audio was recorded with the photos, the wettest reading per material per room is pointed out for confirmation by voice or tap; the rest stay unconfirmed (U) but remain backed by their original photos. Photo analysis is limited to what it does well: equipment, meter displays, room identity, and general progression. Everything else is reviewed by a person, not trusted 100%.

Cabinet parts are named as cabinet parts (cabinet base or bottom panel, toe kick, side panel, interior), never as floor.

HDF-core floating floor isn't salvageable once wet. It comes out across the wet extent, to the transitions, plus a margin past the last wet reading.

text.decision_guidance: On a concrete slab, knock the tile before the remove-or-leave call (Knock Test). Also weigh dwell time, whether the customer wants to save the tile, and the installation method (especially a liner or uncoupling membrane).
text.knock_test: Knock the tile on a concrete slab. A hollow sound means voids or grooves in the mortar where water can sit; on Category 3, remove it. A solid sound usually means there is no space for water to go; removal is not required.
text.voice_note: Tile over concrete: knock it. Hollow means voids or grooves in the mortar where water can sit: on Category 3, take it out. Solid usually means no space for water to go, so removal is not required. Still take it out if there's a smell, or the customer or the company is worried about health and welfare. If it was affected and stays, get a signed release. Don't push removal just to check a box. Write down why.

matrix.description: A structured reference for deciding whether to restore materials in place or remove and replace them. Organized by material type, water category, and approximate dwell time.
matrix.drying_in_place_principle: Drying finish and porous materials in place is Category 1 only (Scoping: Equipment Timing: Drying in Place). On Category 2 or 3, porous and semi-porous finish materials come out. Structure that can't be removed as a finish (framing, slab, structural plywood subfloor, masonry, heavy timber, steel) is cleaned and dried, not a dry-in-place call.

asbestos_floor_layers.text: Thinset, mastic and old self-leveler are asbestos-suspect: sample in Evaluate and hold until clear (Hold Status).

hazard_sampling.description: Older home or suspect material, any age: sample or presume before any destructive work. Sample first and wait: results pending means no disturbing work. Who samples and how many: Hazard Sampling.
hazard_sampling.voice_line: Older home or suspect material: we sample or presume before we cut or demo anything.

pm_asbestos_survey.text: Schedule the asbestos survey before demo. The testing company does the sampling. The state requires it regardless of house age.

scoping_description.text: Universal scope-build rules. Order the scope in execution order; every line resolves to a billable item. No pricing here. Containment scoping default: the home's ceiling is the top; do not scope a poly top (Scoping: Order of Work: Engineering Controls Before Demo: Containment Top).

4. Sink & Toilet Decision: Shut off water supplies. For sinks: disconnect water lines and drain, then install compression caps on the lines. For toilets: shut off water, flush to empty the tank, disconnect supply line, and plug the drain with a drain plug. Toilets come out before the flooring under them. Plumbing caps go on right after any water-line item comes out (dishwasher, fridge, toilet, sink).

5. Appliance Decision: Handle per Demolition: Access Prep: Appliance Handling. Appliances come out before cabinets, around the same time as countertops. Default pull order: refrigerator, range, dishwasher, washing machine, dryer, water heater. Cap water lines as each comes out.

6. Countertop Decision (with appliances, before base cabinets): per Scoping: Countertops: stone almost always off first; cheap top on a non-salvaged particle-board unit goes with the unit; on a salvage cabinet the top comes off first; tile tops ask about bullnose and backsplash. Remove backsplash if present.

9. Walls usually before floors, often the same day; order depends on access and materials. Cut and remove wall and ceiling material (drywall, plaster, or tile wall), then pull all nails and screws from studs and ceiling joists.

11. Flooring Decision, top down: finish floor (carpet, laminate, vinyl, hardwood, tile, glue-down), then underlayment or pad and tack strip, then mud bed / thinset / self-leveler, then subfloor denail and scrape. Thinset, mastic and old self-leveler are asbestos-suspect: sample in Evaluate and hold until clear.
12. After all demo: framing cleanup and mold cleaning. Trash goes out as needed throughout, not only at the end.

room_sub_lists_and_master: - **Source = each actual room.** Every affected Encircle room gets its own living note titled `Mitigation Scope - <Room> · rev N · updated MM/DD/YY`. Techs check items off there. That room note is the source of truth for that room's scope.
- **Edit in place.** PATCH the same note on each update. Do not create a new note per revision. Dated change blocks inside the note go newest-first at the top; older text below stays untouched.

- **Master = pure rollup.** One note in the ◇ RestoKit room titled `Mitigation Scope - Master · rev N · updated MM/DD/YY`. Master has nothing of its own: it is only the combined room sub lists. Never edit Master directly. The authorized Encircle connector refreshes Master in the same approved pass whenever a room note changes.

- **Job-wide lines** (containment, equipment, multi-room holds) go on a home room's sub list so they roll into Master. Flag which room if ambiguous. Do not invent a second copy of room notes inside ◇ RestoKit.

file_connection.text: Xactimate reads .esx and .chx. XML is the other platform's format. There is no public schema. Xactimate is not required by law. It is the industry default. The one real requirement is XactAnalysis: if the job came through that portal, the estimate usually has to go back through it. The structured scope is the source. flow: 1. The user talks as they walk (pasted transcript after the walk, or short live notes while online).

billable_catalog.description: Every billable line the kit knows, in sheet order: what it is, its unit, what it includes or excludes, and why it is billed (the reason id points at the kit section that explains it). The billable mitigation sheet is rendered from this list.
billable_catalog.how_numbering_works: Line numbers are not stored. They come from list order when the sheet is rendered: one running count through the sheet sections, a separate G count for company gap lines, and a dash for open items. Notes and transcription notes cite lines by item id in double braces, and rendering swaps in the current number. Adding, removing or moving an item renumbers the sheet with no gaps and no reserved rows.

item_fields.id: Short readable id, same rules as pointer_index. Never shown to readers; always expanded to the line text.
item_fields.section: Section id the line renders in.
item_fields.label: Line text as printed on the sheet.
item_fields.unit: Billing unit as printed on the sheet.
item_fields.options: Options or instructions column (sheet sections only).
item_fields.cat3: True when the line carries the Cat 3 mark.
item_fields.note: Notes column; inclusions, exclusions and include-or-never-both rules. Line citations are written as item ids in double braces.
item_fields.origin: source_sheet = transcribed from the company sheet; kit_gap = added by the kit (G lines).
item_fields.reason: Id(s) of the kit section that says why this is billed and what it covers.
item_fields.needs_reason: True when no kit section explains the line yet. The line still bills; it is listed for review.
item_fields.status: open = no billable line yet; renders with a dash and no number.

render_rules: Walk layout in order. A text block prints as written after swapping each item id in double braces for that item's current number.
A section block prints its heading with {range} filled from the first and last numbered item in it, then its before_table text, then the table header, separator and one row per item in list order.
Rows use the row template for the section's table format. Empty fields print empty. cat3 prints **3** when true.
Numbers: one running count through sheet sections in section order; G1, G2 and so on for company gap lines; a dash for open items.
A section with no items is skipped.
Readers never see item ids. Agents and the site always print the line text or the rendered number.
No prices. Billing amounts belong to the company sheet and its pricing, not the kit.

scoping.title: Scoping: Order of Work and Billable Logic
scoping.description: Universal scope-build rules. Order the scope in execution order; every line resolves to a billable item. No pricing here. Containment scoping default: the home's ceiling is the top; do not scope a poly top (Scoping: Order of Work: Engineering Controls Before Demo: Containment Top).

tracks.rule: Only two tracks: Living Space and crawlspace.

extraction_first.rule: Extraction comes before contents and plastic in every category.
extraction_first.contents_exception: Contents move first only if they block the water path.
extraction_first.sewage: Sewage pump-out may need containment first (Equipment Setup: Containment First Exceptions).
extraction_first.cat3_crawl: In a Cat 3 crawl the hose breaks the hatch containment; use heavier path protection along the hose route instead.
extraction_first.resolves: Extraction comes before contents protection in Phase 1.

engineering_controls_before_demo.rule: Engineering controls go in before any demo: 6 mil, 4 mil, HEPA negative air, floor protection, painter's plastic.
engineering_controls_before_demo.containment_top: Scoping default: containment uses the home's ceiling as the top. Do not scope a poly top.
engineering_controls_before_demo.flag: Commonly missed: call it out on every scope.
engineering_controls_before_demo.exception: Anything the lead names, e.g. an appliance that won't fit out once the plastic is up.

appliances_and_caps.rule: Appliances come out before cabinets, around the same time as countertops.
appliances_and_caps.caps: Plumbing caps go on right after any water-line item comes out (dishwasher, fridge, toilet).

trim_and_toilets.trim: Trim can come off any time before drywall.
trim_and_toilets.toilets: Toilets come out before the flooring under them.

flooring_top_down.asbestos: Thinset, mastic and old self-leveler are asbestos-suspect: sample in Evaluate and hold until clear (Hold Status).

order_of_work.walls_before_floors: Walls usually come out before floors, often the same day. Order depends on access and materials.
order_of_work.after_demo: Framing cleanup and mold cleaning come after all demo. Trash goes out as needed.

equipment_timing.afd_or_hepa_scrubber: At the start of demo (earlier if mold is seen); stays through cleaning.

countertops.cheap_top_non_salvage: A cheap top on a particle-board unit that isn't salvaged gets trashed with the unit.
countertops.salvage_cabinet: On a salvage cabinet the top comes off first.
countertops.tile: Gray area: ask about bullnose and backsplash.
countertops.gold_standard: A decision per component (top, base, tile, concrete), plus a crew note when they move as one unit.

scoping.toe_kick_salvage: On salvage cabinets: remove the toe kick and drill holes so the cavity can dry. Skip if the cabinet is trashed or has mold.

billing_rules.salvage_deconstruction: Bill salvage deconstruction separately from tear-out.
billing_rules.ppe: PPE is billed by the book, based on category and demo size.
billing_rules.no_double_bill: One physical step = one line (e.g. crawl insulation used to soak up pools is one step).

order: Vapor barrier per function and situation (insulation work needs a good barrier)
crawlspace_track.fast_leak: Pulled insulation can soak up pools, but that is one step: don't bill it twice.
billable: flex duct wrap removal (its own item)
crawlspace_track.optional_forced_air_package: At the hatch (setup, zipper, AFD) when justified.
crawlspace_track.dehumidifier: At the hatch with lay-flat duct for circular airflow.

close.trade_walk: Trade walk on every job before rebuild: electrician and plumber for living space; plumber only for crawl.
close.post_demo_walk: An offer of another inspection, not a requirement.
